01Security (Part 1)

Encoding vs Encryption vs Tokenization

Teeno kaam ek jaise lagte hain — data ko kisi aur form me badal dena. Par inka purpose bilkul alag hai: ek readability ke liye, ek secrecy ke liye, aur ek data ko bina dikhaye use karne ke liye. Interview me ye confusion sabse zyada pakdi jati hai.

1. Teeno ko ek kahani se samjho

Encoding — ek message ko Hindi se English letters me likhna (transliteration). Koi bhi wapas padh sakta hai, koi secret nahi. Bas format badla hai taaki system samajh sake.

Encryption — message ko ek taale me band karke chabhi sirf dost ko dena. Bina chabhi ke koi nahi padh sakta. Chabhi kho gayi to message hamesha ke liye band.

Tokenization — apna asli credit card bank ke locker me rakh ke, uski jagah ek nakli number (token) jeb me rakhna. Dukaan ko nakli number do, wo bank se asli wala nikal le. Nakli number chori bhi ho jaye to koi fayda nahi — asli card locker me safe hai.

Ek line me: Encoding = format badlo (reversible, no secret). Encryption = chabhi se band karo (reversible, secret key). Tokenization = asli data hata ke nakli reference do (original vault me, token ka koi matlab nahi).

2. Gehrai me samjho — ek-ek point

Encoding — format badlo

Encoding ka kaam hai data ko ek system se doosre system tak safely pahunchaane layak banana. Isme koi secret nahi hota — algorithm sabko pata hota hai, aur koi bhi decode kar sakta hai.

Examples: Base64 (binary data ko text me — email attachments, JWT), URL encoding (%20 for space), UTF-8 (characters ko bytes me), Hex encoding.

Hello → Base64 → SGVsbG8= — koi bhi online decoder se wapas 'Hello' padh lega. Isliye encoding security nahi hai — password ko Base64 me store karna bilkul galat hai.

Galat: Password ko Base64 encode karke database me rakhna — ye 'encryption' nahi, ye sirf dikhawa hai.

Encryption — chabhi se band karo

Encryption ka kaam hai data ko unauthorized logon se chhupana. Sirf wahi padh sakta hai jiske paas key hai. Algorithm + secret key, dono chahiye.

Symmetric: Ek hi key se lock aur unlock (AES-256) — fast, par key share karna mushkil. Asymmetric: Public key se lock, private key se unlock (RSA) — key share karna aasan, par slow.

Example: WhatsApp end-to-end encryption — message tumhare phone pe encrypt hota hai, sirf dost ka phone decrypt kar sakta hai. Beech me WhatsApp server bhi nahi padh sakta.

Sahi: Sensitive data (passwords ko hash karo, baaki sensitive data encrypt karo) — key ko alag jagah (KMS/vault) rakho, code me kabhi nahi.

Tokenization — asli data chhupao

Tokenization me sensitive data ko ek random token se replace kar diya jata hai, aur asli data ek secure vault me rehta hai. Token ka asli data se koi mathematical relation nahi hota — isliye token ko reverse-engineer nahi kiya ja sakta.

Example: Card number 4111 1111 1111 1111 → token tok_9f8e7d. Dukaan sirf token store karti hai. Payment karte waqt token vault ko bhejta hai, vault asli card se charge karta hai. Token leak ho jaye to bhi card safe hai.

PCI DSS compliance ke liye tokenization best practice hai — kyunki tumhare system me card number kabhi aata hi nahi, to uska scope bhi kam ho jata hai.

Teeno ka comparison

EncodingEncryptionTokenization
PurposeFormat / transportConfidentialityData ko system se bahar rakhna
Secret?NahiHaan — keyVault me asli data
Reversible?Haan, koi bhiHaan, sirf key seSirf vault se (mapping)
ExampleBase64, UTF-8AES, RSA, TLSCard token, Apple Pay token

Yaad rakhne ka tareeka: Encoding = 'sab padh sakte hain', Encryption = 'sirf key wala padh sakta hai', Tokenization = 'padhne layak kuch hai hi nahi, asli cheez vault me hai'.

3. Real-world me kahan kya use hota hai?

ScenarioKya use hota haiKyun
Password store karnaHashing (bcrypt/Argon2) + saltPassword kabhi wapas nahi chahiye — sirf match check karna hai
API se binary data bhejnaBase64 encodingJSON sirf text handle karta hai
Chat messages (WhatsApp)Encryption (Signal protocol)Sirf sender-receiver padh sakein
Card payments (PCI DSS)TokenizationCard number tumhare system me aaye hi na
Database me PII (Aadhaar, phone)Encryption at rest (AES-256)DB leak ho to bhi data na padha jaye
Hashing vs Encryption — mat bhoolna: Hashing one-way hoti hai (password wapas nahi milta), encryption two-way (key se wapas milta hai). Password ke liye hamesha hashing, baaki sensitive data ke liye encryption.

4. Try karo — teeno ko khud badlo

Ek hi text 'Hello123' ko teeno tareekon se badlo aur dekho kya farq padta hai — kaunsa wapas aata hai, kaunsa nahi?

5. Kab kya use karo — decision table

Agar tumhe...To use karo
Data ko ek format se doosre me badalna hai (binary → text)Encoding (Base64/UTF-8)
Data ko chhupana hai, par baad me wapas chahiyeEncryption (AES/RSA)
Sensitive data ko apne system me rakhna hi nahi haiTokenization
Password verify karna hai, password wapas nahi chahiyeHashing + salt (bcrypt/Argon2)

6. Common galtiyan — ye mat karna

  1. Encoding ko encryption samajhna: Base64 password 'secure' nahi hai — ye beginner ki sabse common galti hai, interview me turant pakdi jati hai.
  2. Encryption ke liye khud ka algorithm banana: 'Maine apna cipher banaya' — kabhi mat karo. AES/RSA jaise tested algorithms use karo; custom crypto hamesha tootta hai.
  3. Key ko code ya config me hardcode karna: Key leak hui to encryption bekaar. KMS, vault ya environment variable use karo.
  4. Password encrypt karke store karna: Password ko hash karo (one-way), encrypt nahi — encrypt kiya to key leak hote hi saare passwords khul jaayenge.
  5. Token ko sensitive data samajh ke encrypt karna: Token ka point hi ye hai ki usme kuch nahi hota — use aise hi store karo, vault ko secure rakho.

7. Interview corner

Q: Encoding aur encryption me farq kya hai?

Encoding sirf format badalta hai, koi secret nahi — koi bhi decode kar sakta hai (Base64). Encryption secret key se data chhupata hai — bina key ke padhna practically impossible (AES). Encoding security nahi hai.

Q: Tokenization encryption se behtar kab hoti hai?

Jab sensitive data tumhare system me aana hi nahi chahiye — jaise card payments. Token ka asli data se koi maths relation nahi hota, to token leak hone se bhi kuch nahi bigadta, aur PCI DSS scope bhi kam ho jata hai.

Q: Password store karne ke liye encryption kyun nahi?

Kyunki password wapas chahiye hi nahi — sirf verify karna hai. Isliye one-way hashing (bcrypt/Argon2 + salt) use hoti hai. Encrypt kiya to key leak hote hi saare passwords expose ho jaayenge.

8. Quick check

Sawaal 1: Kaunsa tareeka security ke liye nahi hai, sirf format badalta hai?

  • AES encryption
  • Tokenization
  • Base64 encoding [sahi jawab]
  • bcrypt hashing

Sawaal 2: Credit card number ko apne system me bilkul na rakhne ke liye kya use karte hain?

  • Base64 encoding
  • Tokenization [sahi jawab]
  • Plain text storage
  • URL encoding
Ek line me yaad rakh lo: Encoding = format (koi secret nahi); Encryption = key se chhupao (wapas milta hai); Tokenization = asli data vault me, token ka koi matlab nahi; Password ke liye hashing + salt.
Source:https://github.com/ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/blob/main/data/guides/encoding-vs-encryption-vs-tokenization.md

02Security (Part 1)

Storing Passwords Safely: A Comprehensive Guide

Database leak hona if nahi, when hai — badi-badi companies ka data leak ho chuka hai. Farq sirf itna hai: password sahi tareeke se store hue the ya nahi. Sahi tareeka ek hi hai — hash + salt, slow algorithm se. Is page me poora flow samjho.

1. Password store karna — bank locker wali kahani

Socho tum ek bank ho. Customer apna password tumhe deta hai. Tum use ek kagaz pe likh ke drawer me rakh do — chor aaya to saare password ek saath le gaya. Ye plain text storage hai, aur ye crime ke barabar hai.

Samajhdar bank kya karta hai? Password ko ek one-way machine (hash) me daalta hai — machine se ek fixed fingerprint nikalta hai, aur asli password phenk deta hai. Har customer ke liye machine me ek chutki namak (salt) bhi daalti hai, taaki do logon ka same password bhi alag fingerprint de. Chor fingerprint chura bhi le to usse password wapas nahi bana sakta — use har password ke liye arabon guesses karne padenge, aur slow machine use aur slow kar deti hai.

Golden rule: Password kabhi store mat karo — sirf uska salted hash store karo, ek slow algorithm (bcrypt / Argon2) se.

2. Gehrai me samjho — ek-ek point

Hashing kya hai?

Hash ek one-way function hai: input → fixed-size fingerprint. hash('hello') hamesha same output dega, par output se input wapas nahi milta. Login ke waqt user jo password deta hai, use dobara hash karo — agar stored hash se match ho gaya to password sahi hai.

Par simple hash (MD5, SHA-256) fast hote hain — aur fast hona yahan bura hai. Attacker ek second me arabon guesses kar sakta hai (brute force / rainbow table). Isliye password ke liye slow, adaptive hash chahiye.

Galat: MD5 ya plain SHA-256 se password hash karna — GPU se billion guesses/second possible hain.

Salt — har password ka apna masala

Salt ek random string hai jo har user ke liye alag hoti hai, aur password ke saath jod ke hash ki jati hai: hash(password + salt). Salt ko hash ke saath hi store karte hain — ye secret nahi hoti.

Salt ke fayde: (1) Do users ka same password (123456) bhi alag hash deta hai — ek hash crack hone se doosra safe. (2) Rainbow table (pehle se computed hash dictionary) bekaar ho jati hai — attacker ko har salt ke liye nayi table banani padegi.

Example: Alice aur Bob dono ka password sunshine hai. Alice ka salt x7!q, Bob ka m2@z — dono ke hash bilkul alag. Attacker ko dono alag-alag crack karne padenge.

bcrypt / Argon2 — slow hi sahi hai

bcrypt (1999) password hashing ka industry standard raha hai: isme cost factor hota hai — jitna cost, utna slow (aur utna secure). Cost 12 matlab ek hash ~250ms leta hai. User ko 250ms ka farq nahi padta, attacker ko arabon guesses me saal lag jaate hain.

Argon2 (2015, Password Hashing Competition winner) aaj ka best choice hai — ye memory-hard bhi hai, matlab GPU/ASIC se bhi fast crack nahi ho sakta. Naye systems me Argon2id use karo; purane systems me bcrypt bhi acceptable hai.

# Python (bcrypt) — sahi tareeka
import bcrypt
hashed = bcrypt.hashpw(password.encode(), bcrypt.gensalt(rounds=12))
# verify: bcrypt.checkpw(password.encode(), hashed)

Poora flow — signup se login tak

Signup: User password deta hai → server random salt banata hai → bcrypt/Argon2 se hash karta hai → DB me sirf username, salt, hash store hota hai. Asli password kahin nahi rehta — memory se bhi turant hata do.

Login: User password deta hai → server stored salt nikaalta hai → same algorithm se hash karta hai → stored hash se compare karta hai (constant-time compare, taaki timing attack na ho). Match = login success.

Password change: Purana password verify karo, phir naya hash banao — purana hash overwrite. Reset: Email pe time-limited token bhejo, password kabhi email pe mat bhejo.

Sahi: Hash ke saath algorithm aur cost bhi store karo (bcrypt string me ye sab embedded hota hai) — taaki aage cost badha sako.

3. Algorithms ka comparison — kaunsa kab?

AlgorithmTypePassword ke liye?Notes
MD5 / SHA-1Fast hash❌ Kabhi nahiBroken + bahut fast — GPU se billion/sec
SHA-256Fast hash❌ Akela nahiData integrity ke liye achha, password ke liye nahi
bcryptSlow, adaptive✅ StandardCost factor badha sakte ho, widely supported
Argon2idSlow + memory-hard✅ Best choice (naye systems)GPU/ASIC resistant, OWASP recommended
PBKDF2Slow, iterated✅ AcceptableNIST approved, par Argon2 se kam strong

Pepper bhi jaan lo: salt ke alawa ek secret value (pepper) jo application ke config/KMS me rehti hai, DB me nahi. DB leak ho to bhi pepper ke bina hash crack nahi hoga. Salt = per-user, public-ish; Pepper = global, secret.

4. Try karo — password crack karne ki koshish karo

Ek leaked database mili hai. Dekho alag-alag storage tareekon me attacker ko kitna time lagega — aur kyun bcrypt jeetta hai.

5. Checklist — password storage ke 8 rules

#RuleKyun
1Plain text kabhi nahiLeak = sab kuch gaya
2Argon2id ya bcrypt use karoSlow + adaptive
3Har user ke liye unique random saltRainbow table bekaar
4MD5/SHA-1 password ke liye kabhi nahiBroken aur bahut fast
5Password ko log mat karoLogs bhi leak hote hain
6HTTPS par hi password bhejoNetwork pe plain password = khel khatam
7Rate limiting + lockout lagaoOnline brute force roko
8Breach hone par users ko force-reset doHash bhi hamesha ke liye safe nahi

6. Common galtiyan — ye mat karna

  1. MD5/SHA-256 se password hash karna: Ye fast hashes hain — attacker GPU se arabon guesses karta hai. Password ke liye slow algorithm chahiye.
  2. Salt ke bina hash karna: Same password = same hash, rainbow table se ek saath saare crack. Har user ka unique salt zaroori hai.
  3. Password encrypt karke rakhna: Encryption reversible hai — key leak hui to saare passwords khul gaye. Hashing one-way hai, isliye sahi hai.
  4. Password ko logs ya error message me print karna: Log files bhi leak hoti hain — password kabhi log mat karo, chahe debugging hi kyun na ho.
  5. Weak password allow karna: '123456' ko bcrypt bhi nahi bacha sakta. Minimum length 8-12, breach-list check (Have I Been Pwned API) aur MFA lagao.

7. Interview corner

Q: Password store karne ka sahi tareeka kya hai?

Plain text ya fast hash (MD5/SHA) kabhi nahi. Har user ke liye unique random salt + slow adaptive hash (Argon2id ya bcrypt, cost factor ke saath) use karo. Verify ke waqt dobara hash karke constant-time compare karo.

Q: Salt aur pepper me farq kya hai?

Salt per-user random value hai, hash ke saath DB me store hoti hai — rainbow table rokti hai. Pepper ek global secret hai jo DB me nahi, app config/KMS me rehta hai — DB leak hone par bhi extra protection deta hai.

Q: bcrypt slow kyun hona chahiye?

Kyunki attacker ko har guess me time lagna chahiye. User ko ek login me 250ms ka farq nahi padta, par attacker ke arabon guesses saalon me badal jaate hain. Cost factor badha ke future hardware se bhi aage raha ja sakta hai.

8. Quick check

Sawaal 1: Password store karne ka sabse sahi tareeka kaunsa hai?

  • Plain text me
  • MD5 hash, bina salt ke
  • bcrypt/Argon2 + unique salt [sahi jawab]
  • Base64 encode karke

Sawaal 2: Salt ka main kaam kya hai?

  • Password ko encrypt karna
  • Har user ka hash alag banana aur rainbow table bekaar karna [sahi jawab]
  • Password ko chhota karna
  • Login ko fast banana
Ek line me yaad rakh lo: Password kabhi store mat karo — sirf salted hash (Argon2id/bcrypt) store karo; salt har user ke liye alag; MD5/SHA password ke liye kabhi nahi; pepper extra layer hai.
Source:https://github.com/ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/blob/main/data/guides/how-to-store-passwords-in-the-database.md

03Security (Part 1)

Designing a Permission System

'Ye user ye kaam kar sakta hai ya nahi?' — ye sawaal har app me hota hai: admin kya dekh sakta hai, editor kya badal sakta hai, viewer sirf padh sakta hai? Permission system wahi jawab dene ka design hai — aur galat design hone par ya to data leak hota hai, ya har feature ke liye code badalna padta hai.

1. Permission system — office building wali kahani

Ek office building me har employee ke paas ek access card hota hai. Card pe uska role likha hota hai — 'Manager', 'Engineer', 'Visitor'. Har darwaze pe likha hota hai kaunsa role andar ja sakta hai. Visitor sirf lobby tak, engineer apni floor tak, manager har floor tak.

Ab socho agar har darwaze pe har employee ka naam likhna padta — 500 log, 100 darwaze, pure din sirf list update karte raho. Isliye roles beech me laaye gaye: user → role → permission → resource. Kisi ki naukri badli to sirf uska role badlo, 100 darwaze nahi.

Core idea: Permission seedha user ko mat do — role ko do, user ko role do. Isse management aasan aur galti kam hoti hai.

2. Gehrai me samjho — ek-ek point

RBAC — Role Based Access Control

RBAC sabse common model hai: permissions roles se judi hoti hain, users ko roles milte hain. Example: Editor role ke paas post:create, post:edit, post:publish hain; Viewer ke paas sirf post:read.

Kaam aise karta hai: request aati hai → user ka role nikalo → role ki permissions check karo → allow ya deny. Permission check har API pe hona chahiye — sirf UI me button chhupana security nahi hai.

Sahi: Permissions ko code me string constants banao (posts:delete) — typo se galti nahi hogi.
Galat: Frontend me 'Delete' button chhupa diya, par API pe koi check nahi — koi bhi curl se delete kar dega.

ABAC — Attribute Based Access Control

Jab sirf role kaafi na ho, attributes aate hain: user ka department, resource ka owner, time, location. Example: 'Doctor sirf apne hospital ke patients ka record dekh sakta hai' — yahan role (doctor) + attribute (hospital_id match) dono chahiye.

ABAC zyada flexible hai, par zyada complex bhi — policy likhni padti hai ('allow if user.dept == resource.dept AND time < 18:00'). Bade systems (AWS IAM, Google Zanzibar) isi taraf jaate hain.

Rule of thumb: Chhote app ke liye RBAC kaafi hai; multi-tenant ya complex rules ke liye ABAC/relationship-based (ReBAC) socho.

Permissions kahan check karein?

Check hamesha server side hona chahiye, har layer pe: API gateway/middleware (route level — kya ye role is endpoint ko call kar sakta hai?), service layer (business logic — kya ye user is document ka owner hai?), data layer (row-level — query me hi filter laga do).

Example: DELETE /posts/123 — middleware check karta hai 'kya user ke paas posts:delete hai?', service check karta hai 'kya post 123 isi user ki hai ya user admin hai?'

Defense in depth: UI pe button chhupana UX hai, security nahi. Asli check API pe hota hai.

Design karte waqt ke decisions

1) Permission granularity: Mote (posts:manage) ya bareek (posts:create/edit/delete/publish)? Bareek zyada control deta hai, par manage karna mushkil. Shuruaat me resource:action format rakho.

2) Role hierarchy: Admin > Editor > Viewer — upar wala neeche wale ke saare rights inherit kare? Simple hai, par kabhi-kabhi galat allow ho jata hai.

3) Permission storage: DB me roles/permissions tables banao (admin panel se badal sakein), code me hardcode mat karo — har naye role ke liye deploy nahi karna chahiye.

4) Audit log: Har allow/deny (khaas karke deny aur sensitive allow) log karo — breach ke baad yahi batayega kisne kya kiya.

3. Database design — tables kaise dikhti hain?

-- RBAC ki classic 5 tables
users        (id, name, email)
roles        (id, name)              -- admin, editor, viewer
permissions  (id, name)              -- posts:create, posts:delete
user_roles   (user_id, role_id)
role_permissions (role_id, permission_id)

-- Check: kya user 42 post delete kar sakta hai?
SELECT 1 FROM user_roles ur
JOIN role_permissions rp ON rp.role_id = ur.role_id
JOIN permissions p ON p.id = rp.permission_id
WHERE ur.user_id = 42 AND p.name = 'posts:delete';

Performance ke liye user ki permissions ko login ke waqt JWT ya session me cache karo — har request pe 3-table join mat karo. Par role badle to cache invalidate karna mat bhoolo (short expiry ya version number use karo).

4. Try karo — access control ka faisla karo

Alag-alag users alag kaam karne ki koshish karte hain. System ka faisla dekho — allow hoga ya deny, aur kyun?

5. RBAC vs ABAC vs ACL — kab kya?

ModelKaiseBest forMushkil
RBACUser → Role → PermissionMost apps, teams, SaaSFine-grained rules mushkil
ABACAttributes + policiesMulti-tenant, healthcare, financePolicy likhna complex
ACLHar resource pe user listFile sharing (Google Drive)Bade scale pe manage mushkil
ReBACRelationships (Zanzibar)Social apps, Drive jaisi sharingGraph maintain karna

6. Common galtiyan — ye mat karna

  1. Sirf UI me button chhupana: Ye security nahi, UX hai. API pe check nahi hoga to koi bhi direct request bhej dega.
  2. Permissions ko code me hardcode karna: Har naye role ke liye deploy karna padega. Roles/permissions DB me rakho, admin panel se manage karo.
  3. 'Admin sab kuch kar sakta hai' ko default banana: Admin ka bhi audit log hona chahiye, aur admin count kam se kam rakhna chahiye (least privilege).
  4. Role change ke baad purana token/cache valid rehne dena: Role badla, par JWT me purani permissions 1 ghante tak valid — is dauraan user galat kaam kar sakta hai. Short expiry ya revocation rakho.
  5. Deny ko log na karna: Baar-baar deny hona attack ka signal ho sakta hai (koi probe kar raha hai). Audit log me allow + deny dono rakho.

7. Interview corner

Q: RBAC kya hai aur ye kyun popular hai?

Role Based Access Control: permissions roles ko milti hain, users ko roles milte hain. Ye popular hai kyunki manage karna aasan hai — role badlo, 100 jagah update nahi karni padti. Most SaaS apps ke liye kaafi hai.

Q: Frontend pe button chhupana security kyun nahi hai?

Kyunki attacker browser se nahi, direct API request se attack karta hai. Asli authorization check hamesha server side (API/service layer) pe hona chahiye; UI sirf experience ke liye hai.

Q: ABAC kab use karna chahiye?

Jab sirf role kaafi na ho — jaise 'doctor sirf apne hospital ke patients dekhe'. Yahan attributes (department, ownership, time) bhi decide karte hain. Multi-tenant aur regulated systems me ABAC zaroori ho jata hai.

8. Quick check

Sawaal 1: Permission system me user ko seedha permission dene ke bajay kya use karte hain?

  • Seedha database access
  • Role — user ko role, role ko permission [sahi jawab]
  • Sirf password
  • Kuch nahi, sabko sab kuch

Sawaal 2: Authorization check sabse important kahan hona chahiye?

  • Sirf frontend UI me
  • Server side API/service layer pe [sahi jawab]
  • CSS file me
  • Kahin nahi
Ek line me yaad rakh lo: User → Role → Permission: roles beech me rakhne se management aasan; check hamesha server side pe; RBAC most apps ke liye, ABAC complex rules ke liye; least privilege aur audit log mat bhoolo.

DAC aur MAC — guide ke baaki 2 models

Guide me kul 5 tareeke hain — ACL, DAC, MAC, ABAC, RBAC. Upar RBAC aur ABAC aa gaye; DAC aur MAC ye rahe:

  • DAC — Discretionary Access Control: ACL par based hai. Object ka owner (ya owner group) decide karta hai ki kis ko access mile. Fayda: easy aur flexible — Linux file system DAC hi use karta hai. Nuksaan: permission control bikhar jata hai, aur object ke owner ke paas bahut zyada power aa jati hai.
  • MAC — Mandatory Access Control: resource owners aur resources dono ke classification labels hote hain. Alag labels ko alag permissions milti hain. Fayda: strict aur straightforward. Nuksaan: flexible nahi hai — har cheez label se bandhi hoti hai.

Yaad rakhne ka tareeka: ACL = list, DAC = owner decide kare, MAC = label decide kare, RBAC = role decide kare, ABAC = attributes decide karein.

Source:https://github.com/ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/blob/main/data/guides/how-do-we-design-a-permission-system.md

04Security (Part 1)

How Password Managers Work

Har site ka alag, mazboot password yaad rakhna impossible hai — isliye log ek hi password har jagah use karte hain, aur ek leak se sab kuch chala jata hai. Password manager (1Password, LastPass, Bitwarden) is problem ko solve karta hai: ek master password yaad rakho, baaki sab wo sambhalta hai — par wo tumhare passwords ko kaise safe rakhta hai?

1. Password manager — ek aisa tijori jiska taala sirf tum khol sakte ho

Socho tumhare paas ek tijori (vault) hai jisme 200 chabhiyan (passwords) padi hain. Tijori ki chabhi (master password) sirf tumhare paas hai — company ke paas bhi nahi. Tijori ko koi chura bhi le to andar ki chabhiyan ek coded bhasha me likhi hain, jise sirf tumhari chabhi padh sakti hai.

Password manager wahi karta hai: tumhare saare passwords ek encrypted vault me store hote hain. Vault ko kholne wali key tumhare master password se banti hai, aur wo key kabhi company ke server par nahi jati. Isliye company khud bhi tumhare passwords nahi padh sakti — isse zero-knowledge architecture kehte hain.

Zero-knowledge ka matlab: Server pe sirf encrypted blob rehta hai. Decrypt karne ki key sirf tumhare device pe banti hai. Server hack ho jaye to bhi passwords safe hain.

2. Gehrai me samjho — ek-ek point

Master password se key kaise banti hai?

Master password seedha encryption key nahi banta — use key derivation function (KDF) se guzara jata hai: PBKDF2, Argon2 ya scrypt. Ye jaan-bujh ke slow hota hai (lakhon iterations) taaki attacker har guess me time lagaye.

Flow: Master password + random salt → KDF (100k+ iterations) → Master Key. Phir Master Key se ek random Vault Key encrypt hoti hai, aur Vault Key se har password encrypt hota hai (AES-256). Ye two-layer design isliye hai taaki master password badle to sirf Vault Key dobara encrypt karni pade, saare 200 passwords dobara nahi.

1Password me ek extra Secret Key bhi hoti hai — 128-bit random value jo sirf tumhare device pe rehti hai. Master password + Secret Key dono chahiye, to sirf password guess karna kaafi nahi.

Autofill kaise kaam karta hai?

Jab tum kisi site pe login karte ho, browser extension domain check karta hai: vault me github.com ka password hai? Haan to wo username/password fields me bhar deta hai — tumhe copy-paste nahi karna padta.

Domain matching yahan security feature hai: agar tum githb.com (fake site) pe ho, to manager autofill nahi karega — kyunki domain match nahi hua. Isse phishing attack bhi rukta hai: fake site ko asli password kabhi nahi milta.

Sahi: Manager sirf exact domain pe autofill kare — ye phishing se bachne ka sabse aasan tareeka hai.
Galat: Password manager se password copy karke kisi bhi site pe paste karna — domain check bypass ho jata hai.

Password generate karna

Manager har site ke liye ek random, lamba, unique password banata hai — jaise X7#kP9!mQ2$vL8&nR4. Tumhe yaad rakhne ki zaroorat nahi, isliye lamba aur random hona koi problem nahi.

Ye passwords cryptographically secure random generator se bante hain (Math.random() nahi!). Length 16-20 characters, mixed case + numbers + symbols. Aisa password brute-force karna practically impossible hai.

Bonus: manager purane/leaked passwords bhi batata hai — agar tumhara password kisi breach me mila hai (Have I Been Pwned data se), to wo warn karta hai: 'Ye password badlo!'

Sync aur sharing kaise safe hai?

Vault encrypt hokar server pe sync hota hai. Tum phone pe password badlo, laptop pe encrypted blob update hota hai, laptop pe tumhara master password use decrypt karta hai. Server ko kabhi plain password nahi dikhta.

Sharing: Family/Team plan me password share karna ho to manager use receiver ki public key se encrypt karke bhejta hai — sirf receiver ki private key use khol sakti hai. Server beech me sirf courier hai.

Emergency access: Agar tum bhool jao to? Master password bhool gaye to company bhi nahi khol sakti (zero-knowledge!). Isliye recovery kit / emergency contact pehle se set karna zaroori hai.

3. Andar ka architecture — ek table me

LayerKya hota haiAlgorithm
Master password → KeyKey derivation, slow + saltedArgon2 / PBKDF2 (100k+ iterations)
Vault keyRandom 256-bit key, master key se encryptedAES-256
Har password entryVault key se encryptedAES-256-GCM
Server storageSirf encrypted blobZero-knowledge
SharingReceiver ki public key se encryptRSA / X25519

LastPass breach (2022) se seekh: Attackers ne encrypted vaults chura liye. Jinka master password mazboot tha, wo safe rahe; kamzor master password wale crack ho gaye. Matlab: master password hi sabse kamzor kadi hai — use lamba, unique rakho aur MFA on karo.

4. Try karo — vault kholo aur autofill dekho

Tumhara vault lock hai. Master password daalo, vault kholo, phir alag-alag sites pe autofill try karo — dekho fake site pe kya hota hai.

5. Password manager vs browser save vs yaad rakhna

TareekaSecurityConvenience
Ek password har jagah❌ Ek leak = sab gayaYaad rakhna aasan
Browser me save (Chrome)⚠ Theek, par zero-knowledge nahi hotaBuilt-in, aasan
Dedicated manager✅ Zero-knowledge, cross-deviceEk master password yaad rakho
Diary me likhna❌ Chori/physical riskOffline

6. Common galtiyan — ye mat karna

  1. Kamzor master password rakhna: Poora vault ek password pe tikka hai — 'password123' matlab vault khula pada hai. Lamba passphrase (4-5 random words) use karo.
  2. Master password bhool jana: Zero-knowledge me company bhi recover nahi kar sakti. Recovery kit ko safe jagah (printed, locker me) rakho.
  3. MFA on na karna: Manager account pe 2FA zaroor lagao — master password leak bhi ho to second factor bacha lega.
  4. Har site pe autofill blindly allow karna: Sirf trusted domains pe autofill karo; nayi/ajeeb domain pe pehle URL check karo.
  5. Manager ko hi sab kuch de dena bina backup ke: Vault ka encrypted export backup rakho — service band ho ya account lock ho to bhi access rahe.

7. Interview corner

Q: Password manager zero-knowledge kaise hota hai?

Encryption key master password se sirf user ke device pe banti hai; server pe sirf encrypted blob jata hai. Company ke paas key nahi hoti, to wo passwords padh hi nahi sakti — server hack bhi ho jaye to vault safe rehta hai.

Q: Master password se seedha password encrypt kyun nahi karte?

Kyunki master password badalne par saare passwords dobara encrypt karne padte. Two-layer design me ek random Vault Key saare passwords encrypt karti hai, aur master key sirf Vault Key ko encrypt karti hai — password badlo to sirf ek key dobara encrypt hoti hai.

Q: Password manager phishing se kaise bachata hai?

Autofill sirf exact domain match par hota hai. Fake site (githb.com) par manager password bharta hi nahi — kyunki domain vault entry se match nahi karta. User ko password dikhta bhi nahi, to wo galti se bhi fake site ko de nahi sakta.

8. Quick check

Sawaal 1: Password manager me tumhare passwords server par kis form me rehte hain?

  • Plain text me
  • Encrypted blob — key sirf tumhare paas [sahi jawab]
  • Base64 me
  • Company ke employees padh sakte hain

Sawaal 2: Fake website (phishing) par password manager kya karta hai?

  • Password bhar deta hai
  • Domain match na hone par autofill refuse karta hai [sahi jawab]
  • Password email kar deta hai
  • Kuch nahi karta
Ek line me yaad rakh lo: Ek master password yaad rakho, baaki manager sambhalta hai; vault zero-knowledge encrypted hota hai (key sirf device pe); autofill sirf exact domain pe — phishing se bhi bachata hai; master password mazboot rakho.

Andar ki key chain — MUK se vault tak

Guide ke steps 1–6 me poori key chain hai — ye woh detail hai jo vault ko zero-knowledge banati hai:

  1. Step 1 — Signup: email + account password daalo. Password manager tumhare liye ek secret key generate karta hai. Email, account password aur secret key — in 3 fields se MUK (Master Unlock Key) aur SRP-X bante hain, 2SKD algorithm se. Secret key sirf tumhare device par store hoti hai — server ko kabhi nahi bheji jati.
  2. Step 2 — MP key: MUK se primary keyset ki encrypted MP key banti hai.
  3. Steps 3–5 — Private key aur vault key: MP key se private key banti hai; private key se doosre keysets ke AES keys aur vault key banti hai. Vault server par tumhare items (passwords, notes) ka collection store karta hai.
  4. Step 6 — Vault encryption: vault key se vault ke items encrypt hote hain.

Iska matlab: itni lambi chain ki wajah se password manager ke paas tumhare passwords padhne ka koi tareeka hi nahi hai — tumhe sirf ek account password yaad rakhna hai, baaki sab wo yaad rakhta hai.

Source:https://github.com/ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/blob/main/data/guides/how-does-a-password-manager-such-as-1password-or-lastpass-work.md
← PichhlaDesigning a Permission SystemAgla →Firewall Explained to Kids and Adults
05Security (Part 1)

Firewall Explained to Kids and Adults

Internet ek bheed-bhaad wala bazaar hai — achhe log bhi hain, chor bhi. Firewall tumhare ghar (network/computer) ke gate pe khada security guard hai: har aane-jaane wale ko check karta hai, list dekh ke decide karta hai — andar aane do ya bahar roko.

1. Firewall — ghar ke gate wala guard

Bachchon ke liye: Socho tumhare ghar ke gate pe ek guard khada hai jiske paas ek list hai. List me likha hai: 'Doodh wala andar aa sakta hai, dost andar aa sakta hai, ajaan aadmi nahi.' Guard har aane wale ko list se match karta hai. Jo list me nahi, wo bahar hi rukta hai.

Badon ke liye: Firewall network traffic ko rules ke hisaab se filter karta hai — source IP, destination port, protocol. Rule match hua to allow, nahi to deny/drop. Ye network layer pe kaam karta hai: har packet ko dekhta hai, uska header padhta hai, aur faisla karta hai.

Ek line me: Firewall = traffic filter. Har packet ko rule se match karo — allow ya block. Default deny sabse safe policy hai: jo explicitly allow nahi, wo block.

2. Gehrai me samjho — ek-ek point

Packet filtering — pehli peedhi

Sabse simple firewall: har packet ka header dekhta hai — source IP, destination IP, port, protocol (TCP/UDP). Rule se match karo: 'Port 80 (HTTP) allow, baaki sab block'.

Ye fast aur sasta hai, par stateless hota hai: har packet ko alag dekhta hai, context nahi jaanta. Isliye attacker packet ko tod-marod ke bhej sakta hai, aur ye ye nahi jaanta ki packet kisi pehle se chalu connection ka hissa hai ya nahi.

Example rule: ALLOW TCP from any to 192.168.1.10:443 — matlab koi bhi mere web server ke HTTPS port pe aa sakta hai, baaki ports band.

Stateful firewall — dimaag wala guard

Stateful firewall connection ki state yaad rakhta hai. Jab tumhari computer kisi site se connect karti hai, wo entry note karta hai: '192.168.1.5 ne google.com:443 se connection khola hai'. Jab jawab aata hai, wo check karta hai — ye kisi jaani-pehchani connection ka jawab hai? Haan to allow, nahi to block.

Isse bahar se aane wale random packets apne aap block ho jaate hain — kyunki tumne pehle unse baat hi nahi ki thi. Aaj ke zyadatar firewalls (ghar ke router se leke AWS Security Groups tak) stateful hain.

Sahi: Default deny + sirf zaroori ports kholo. Har khula port ek darwaza hai — jitne kam darwaze, utni kam chori.

Next-Gen Firewall (NGFW) — andar bhi dekhta hai

NGFW sirf header nahi, packet ke andar bhi dekhta hai (deep packet inspection): ye kaunsi application hai (Facebook? YouTube?), isme malware hai? Ye IPS (Intrusion Prevention), application control aur threat intelligence ko ek box me jodta hai.

Example: Rule 'Facebook allow, par file upload block' — sirf port dekh ke ye nahi ho sakta, packet ke andar dekhna padta hai. Palo Alto, Fortinet jaise NGFW yehi karte hain.

Cloud me yehi kaam Security Groups (AWS) aur WAF (Web Application Firewall — HTTP attacks jaise SQL injection rokti hai) karte hain.

Firewall kahan-kahan hota hai?

Network firewall: Router ya alag box — poore office/ghar ke network ko protect karta hai. Host firewall: Tumhare laptop pe (Windows Firewall, iptables) — sirf us machine ko protect karta hai.

Cloud firewall: AWS Security Groups / NACLs — virtual network ke rules. WAF: Web app ke saamne — SQL injection, XSS jaise HTTP attacks rokti hai.

Ye layers ek saath kaam karte hain — defense in depth: ek layer chook gayi to doosri pakad legi. Sirf ek firewall pe bharosa mat karo.

3. Firewall rules — kaise likhe jaate hain?

# iptables (Linux host firewall) — simple rules
iptables -P INPUT DROP            # default: sab block
iptables -A INPUT -i lo -j ACCEPT # apne aap se baat allow
iptables -A INPUT -m conntrack --ctstate ESTABLISHED,RELATED -j ACCEPT
iptables -A INPUT -p tcp --dport 22 -s 203.0.113.5 -j ACCEPT  # SSH sirf office IP se
iptables -A INPUT -p tcp --dport 443 -j ACCEPT                # HTTPS sabko
# Ab: SSH sirf office se, HTTPS sabko, baaki sab BLOCK

Rules ka order matter karta hai: Firewall rules ko upar se neeche check karta hai — pehla match jeetta hai. Isliye specific rules upar, general rules neeche, aur aakhir me default deny.

4. Try karo — firewall guard bano

Tum firewall ho. Alag-alag packets aate hain — rules dekh ke decide karo: ALLOW ya BLOCK?

5. Firewall ke types — ek table me

TypeKya dekhta haiStrengthKamzori
Packet-filteringHeader (IP/port)Fast, sastaStateless, aasan bypass
StatefulHeader + connection stateZyada securePayload nahi dekhta
Proxy firewallPoora request (beech me khada)Deep controlSlow, complex
NGFWHeader + payload + appMalware/IPS bhiMehenga
WAFHTTP layer attacksSQLi/XSS rokta haiSirf web apps ke liye

6. Common galtiyan — ye mat karna

  1. Default allow rakhna: 'Sab allow, sirf kharab cheez block' — tum har naye attack ko pehle se nahi jaante. Default deny rakho: sirf jo chahiye, wahi allow.
  2. Saare ports khol dena: 'Testing ke liye 0.0.0.0/0 khol diya' aur bhool gaye — attacker ko khula darwaza mil gaya. Har rule ki expiry/review date rakho.
  3. Firewall ko hi kaafi samajhna: Firewall network layer pe hai — phishing email ya weak password ko nahi rokta. Ye ek layer hai, poori security nahi.
  4. Rules ka order galat rakhna: Pehla match jeetta hai — broad 'allow all' upar rakh diya to neeche ke block rules kabhi check hi nahi honge.
  5. Logs kabhi na dekhna: Block hue packets me attack ki kahani hoti hai. Logs ko monitor karo, alerts lagao — warna firewall andhere me kaam kar raha hai.

7. Interview corner

Q: Firewall kya karta hai?

Firewall network traffic ko rules ke hisaab se filter karta hai — har packet ka source/destination/port dekh ke allow ya block karta hai. Stateful firewall connection ki state bhi yaad rakhta hai, NGFW packet ke andar (payload) bhi dekhta hai.

Q: Stateful aur stateless firewall me farq?

Stateless har packet ko alag dekhta hai, context nahi jaanta. Stateful connection table maintain karta hai — sirf un packets ko allow karta hai jo pehle se chalu connection ka hissa hain ya nayi allowed connection shuru karte hain.

Q: Firewall aur WAF me farq?

Firewall network/transport layer pe kaam karta hai (IP/port). WAF application layer (HTTP) pe — SQL injection, XSS jaise web attacks ko rokta hai. Dono alag layers, dono chahiye.

8. Quick check

Sawaal 1: Firewall ka sabse safe default rule kaunsa hai?

  • Sab kuch allow karo
  • Default deny — sirf jo chahiye wahi allow [sahi jawab]
  • Sirf port 80 kholo
  • Koi rule mat banao

Sawaal 2: Stateful firewall kya yaad rakhta hai?

  • Sirf password
  • Connection ki state — kaunsi connection pehle se chalu hai [sahi jawab]
  • User ka naam
  • Website ka design
Ek line me yaad rakh lo: Firewall = gate pe guard: packet ko rules se match karke allow/block; stateful = connection yaad rakhta hai; NGFW = payload bhi dekhta hai; default deny sabse safe.

Firewall ke types — poori list

Guide ke hisaab se firewall 2 broad categories me aate hain:

  • Software-based: individual device par install hota hai, usi device ki raksha karta hai.
  • Hardware-based: alag stand-alone device hota hai, poore network ki raksha karta hai.

Types — ek-ek karke:

  • Packet Filtering Firewall: packet ko source, destination ya protocol dekh kar accept ya reject karta hai.
  • Circuit-level Gateway: packets ke beech TCP handshake ko monitor karta hai, taaki session ki legitimacy (asliyat) check kar sake — handshake poora nahi hua to session aage nahi badhta.
  • Application-level Gateway (Proxy Firewall): tumhare network aur traffic source ke beech traffic filter karta hai — untrusted network se ek protective shield banata hai.
  • Stateful Inspection Firewall: active connections ko track karta hai aur packet ko uske data stream me jagah ke context me allow karta hai.
  • Next-Generation Firewall (NGFW): purane tareekon ke saath intrusion prevention, deep packet analysis aur application awareness jod deta hai.
Source:https://github.com/ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/blob/main/data/guides/firewall-explained-to-kids-and-adults.md
← PichhlaHow Password Managers WorkAgla →HTTP Cookies Explained With a Simple Diagram
06Security (Part 1)

HTTP Cookies Explained With a Simple Diagram

Har baar jab tum website kholte ho, wo tumhe pehchanti kaise hai? Tumne dark mode chuna tha, wo yaad kaise rehta hai? Iske peeche ek chhota sa mechanism hai — HTTP Cookie. Ye page cookies ko shuruaat se, request-response flow ke saath samjhata hai.

1. Cookie — cinema ka ticket stub

Socho tum cinema jaate ho. Counter pe ticket kharidte ho, andar jaate ho. Interval me bahar aate ho — guard tumhe wapas kaise jaane de? Tumhare paas ticket ka stub hai. Guard stub dekhta hai, 'haan, ye andar wala hi hai', aur jaane deta hai.

HTTP cookie wahi stub hai. Pehli baar server tumhe ek cookie deta hai (Set-Cookie header), browser use sambhal ke rakhta hai, aur har baar request ke saath wapas bhejta hai (Cookie header). Server stub dekh ke pehchan leta hai: 'Ye wahi user hai.'

Yaad rakhna: HTTP stateless hai — har request nayi hoti hai. Cookie hi wo yaad hai jo requests ko jodti hai.

2. Gehrai me samjho — ek-ek point

Cookie banti kaise hai? — Set-Cookie

Jab server chahta hai ki browser kuch yaad rakhe, wo response me Set-Cookie header bhejta hai:

HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Set-Cookie: theme=dark; Path=/; Max-Age=2592000
Set-Cookie: session_id=abc123; HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Lax

Browser ye cookies store kar leta hai — har cookie ka naam, value, domain, path aur expiry hoti hai. Agli baar jab browser usi domain ko request bhejta hai, to matching cookies ko Cookie header me jod deta hai.

Domain aur Path: Cookie sirf usi domain (aur path) ko bheji jati hai jiske liye bani thi. example.com ki cookie google.com ko kabhi nahi jayegi.

Cookie wapas kaise jati hai? — Cookie header

Har request ke saath browser automatically cookies bhejta hai — tumhe kuch karna nahi padta:

GET /dashboard HTTP/1.1
Host: example.com
Cookie: theme=dark; session_id=abc123

Server session_id padh ke user ko pehchanta hai, theme padh ke dark mode dikhata hai. Ye sab automatic hai — browser khud karta hai.

Isi liye cookies me zyada data mat rakho: har request ke saath ye data travel karta hai, bandwidth aur latency dono badhti hai.

Cookie ke attributes — har ek ka matlab

AttributeMatlab
Expires / Max-AgeCookie kab tak zinda rahegi. Nahi diya to browser band hote hi khatam (session cookie).
DomainKis domain ko cookie bheji jaye.
PathKis path pe cookie bheji jaye (/admin ki cookie sirf /admin pe).
SecureSirf HTTPS pe bhejo — HTTP pe kabhi nahi.
HttpOnlyJavaScript document.cookie se padh nahi sakta — XSS se bachao.
SameSiteCross-site request pe cookie bhejo ya nahi — CSRF se bachao.

SameSite values: Strict (kabhi cross-site nahi), Lax (sirf top-level GET pe), None (hamesha — par Secure bhi chahiye).

Cookie kahan use hoti hai?

1) Login/session: Session ID cookie me (sabse common). 2) Preferences: Theme, language, currency. 3) Shopping cart: Guest user ka cart. 4) Tracking: Analytics aur ads — third-party cookies (jo browsers ab block kar rahe hain).

GDPR/CCPA: Europe me tracking cookies ke liye user ki consent chahiye — isliye har site pe 'Accept cookies?' wala banner dikhta hai. Zaroori cookies (login) ke liye consent nahi chahiye, tracking ke liye chahiye.

Sahi: Sirf zaroori cookies rakho, har cookie pe Secure + HttpOnly + SameSite lagao.

3. Poora flow — request aur response ke saath

PEHLI VISIT (cookie nahi hai):
Browser → Server: GET /  (koi Cookie header nahi)
Server  → Browser: 200 OK + Set-Cookie: session_id=abc123; HttpOnly; Secure

DOOSRI VISIT (cookie hai):
Browser → Server: GET /dashboard
                    Cookie: session_id=abc123
Server: session store me abc123 dhoondha → user Priya mili
Server  → Browser: 200 OK + "Welcome back, Priya!"

LOGOUT:
Server  → Browser: Set-Cookie: session_id=; Max-Age=0  (cookie delete)
Server: session store se abc123 delete

Cookie delete kaise hoti hai? Server wahi naam ki cookie Max-Age=0 ya purani expiry date ke saath bhejta hai — browser use turant hata deta hai.

4. Try karo — cookie ka safar dekho

Ek browser bano: pehli visit karo, cookie pao, phir har request pe cookie bhejo. Phir ek cross-site request try karo — SameSite kya karta hai?

5. Cookie vs LocalStorage — kab kya?

CheezCookieLocalStorage
Har request pe server ko jati hai?Haan, automaticNahi, sirf JS padhta hai
Size~4KB~5-10MB
ExpiryServer set karta haiManual delete tak rehti hai
XSS se khatra?HttpOnly se bachao possibleJS padh sakta hai — chori possible
Best forSession ID, auth tokenNon-sensitive UI data, cache

Rule: Auth token hamesha HttpOnly cookie me rakho, LocalStorage me nahi — kyunki LocalStorage ko koi bhi XSS script padh sakti hai.

6. Common galtiyan — ye mat karna

  1. Auth token LocalStorage me rakhna: XSS hote hi token chori. HttpOnly cookie use karo — JS use padh hi nahi sakta.
  2. SameSite flag bhoolna: Bina SameSite ke CSRF attack aasan hai. Aaj kal SameSite=Lax minimum hai.
  3. Secure flag ke bina production: HTTP pe cookie plain text me travel karti hai — network pe koi bhi padh sakta hai. Production me hamesha Secure.
  4. Cookie me zyada data bharna: Har request ke saath cookie jati hai — 4KB ki 10 cookies matlab har request pe 40KB extra. Performance kharab hoti hai.
  5. Cookie ko kabhi expire na karna: 'Remember me' ke alawa har cookie ki expiry honi chahiye — chori hui cookie hamesha valid nahi rehni chahiye.

7. Interview corner

Q: Cookie kaise kaam karti hai?

Server response me Set-Cookie header bhejta hai, browser use store karta hai, aur har aane wali request me Cookie header ke saath wapas bhejta hai. Isse stateless HTTP me bhi user ko pehchana ja sakta hai.

Q: HttpOnly aur Secure flag kya karte hain?

HttpOnly JavaScript ko cookie access karne se rokta hai — XSS se session chori nahi hoti. Secure cookie ko sirf HTTPS connection pe bhejta hai — HTTP pe plain-text leak nahi hota.

Q: SameSite cookie CSRF se kaise bachati hai?

SameSite cross-site requests ke saath cookie bhejne se rokta hai. Attacker ki site se bheji gayi request pe browser session cookie nahi bhejega, to server use anonymous maan ke reject kar dega.

8. Quick check

Sawaal 1: Server browser ko cookie kaise deta hai?

  • Cookie header se
  • Set-Cookie response header se [sahi jawab]
  • Email se
  • JavaScript se

Sawaal 2: Auth token ko LocalStorage ke bajay HttpOnly cookie me kyun rakhte hain?

  • Cookie badi hoti hai
  • HttpOnly cookie ko JavaScript/XSS padh nahi sakta [sahi jawab]
  • LocalStorage slow hai
  • Cookie sasti hoti hai
Ek line me yaad rakh lo: Set-Cookie se cookie banti hai, Cookie header se wapas jati hai; HttpOnly (XSS se), Secure (HTTP leak se), SameSite (CSRF se) bachate hain; auth token hamesha HttpOnly cookie me.
Source:https://github.com/ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/blob/main/data/guides/http-cookies-explained-with-a-simple-diagram.md
← PichhlaFirewall Explained to Kids and AdultsAgla →Sessions, Tokens, JWT, SSO, and OAuth Explained
07Security (Part 1)

Sessions, Tokens, JWT, SSO, and OAuth Explained

Login karte waqt peeche kitne concepts kaam karte hain — Session, Token, JWT, SSO, OAuth — aur ye sab aapas me kaise jude hain? Ye page in paanchon ko ek hi badi kahani me jodta hai: ek user, ek login, aur poora internet.

1. Paanch concepts, ek kahani — office campus

Socho ek bada office campus hai jisme kai buildings hain (Gmail, Drive, YouTube — sab Google ki buildings). Tum gate pe ek baar ID dikhate ho (login), aur tumhe ek campus pass milta hai.

Session = gate wale ke register me tumhara naam — wo yaad rakhta hai tum andar ho. Token/JWT = tumhare haath ka pass card — jisme tumhara naam aur expiry likhi hai, gate wala bina register dekhe jaane deta hai. SSO = ek hi pass se saari buildings me entry — har building pe dobara ID nahi dikhani padti. OAuth = tum kisi bahari aadmi (third-party app) ko kehte ho 'meri building me jaa ke mera ek file le aao' — use tumhari chabhi nahi dete, ek limited permission wala pass dete ho.

Yaad rakhne ka tareeka: Session/Token = tum kaun ho (authentication). SSO = ek login, kai apps. OAuth = kisi aur ko apni taraf se kaam karne ki permission (authorization).

2. Gehrai me samjho — ek-ek point

Session — server ka register

Session sabse purana tareeka hai: login ke baad server tumhara record apne paas rakhta hai (Redis/DB), aur tumhe ek session ID deta hai (cookie me). Har request pe server register check karta hai.

Plus: Turant revoke, data server pe safe. Minus: Har request pe lookup, multiple servers pe shared store chahiye.

Single app ke liye session best hai — simple aur control tumhare haath me.

Token aur JWT — khud ka saboot

Token ek signed proof hai: 'ye user #42 hai, ye role hai, ye expiry hai'. JWT iska sabse popular format hai — Header.Payload.Signature.

Server ko kuch yaad nahi rakhna padta — signature verify karo, kaam ho gaya. Isliye JWT APIs aur microservices me chalta hai: har service khud verify kar sakti hai, central session store ki zaroorat nahi.

Trade-off: Revoke mushkil hai — isliye JWT ki expiry chhoti rakho (15 min) aur refresh token alag se use karo.

SSO — ek login, sab apps

SSO (Single Sign-On) matlab ek baar login karo, company ki saari apps (Gmail, Drive, Slack) bina dobara login ke khul jaayein. Peeche Identity Provider (IdP) hota hai — jaise Google, Okta, Azure AD.

Flow: Tum Drive kholte ho → Drive kehta hai 'login nahi ho, IdP pe jao' → IdP pe tum pehle se login ho → IdP ek token (SAML/OIDC) deke wapas bhejta hai → Drive tumhe andar jaane deta hai. Tumhe password dobara nahi dena pada.

Fayda: Ek password yaad rakho, ek jagah MFA lagao, ek jagah se logout (saari apps se). Khatra: IdP hack hua to saari apps khul jaati hain — isliye IdP pe strong MFA zaroori hai.

OAuth — permission dena, password nahi

OAuth 2.0 authorization ka standard hai: tum ek app ko apne data tak limited access dete ho, bina password diye. Example: 'Login with Google' dabate ho, ya ek app ko kehte ho 'mere Google Drive ki files padh lo'.

Flow: App tumhe Google pe bhejti hai → tum kehte ho 'haan, is app ko meri files padhne do' → Google app ko ek access token deta hai (sirf files padhne ka, 1 ghante ke liye) → app token se Drive API call karti hai. Tumhara password app ko kabhi nahi milta, aur tum kabhi bhi permission wapas le sakte ho.

Galat: OAuth ko login samajhna — OAuth authorization hai. Login ke liye uske upar OIDC (OpenID Connect) use hota hai.

3. Sab kuch ek saath — poora flow

USER → APP (pehli baar):
1. User "Login with Google" dabata hai (OAuth + OIDC)
2. App user ko Google (IdP) pe bhejti hai
3. User Google pe login karta hai (password + 2FA)
4. Google app ko authorization code deta hai
5. App code badal ke access token + ID token leti hai
6. ID token (JWT) se user ki pehchan milti hai → APP ME SESSION BANTA HAI
7. Ab user app me session cookie se ghumta hai

SSO (doosri app):
8. User doosri app kholta hai → wahi IdP → pehle se login hai
9. Naya token milta hai → bina password ke login ✓

THIRD-PARTY ACCESS (OAuth):
10. User kisi app ko "Drive files padhne" ki permission deta hai
11. App ko scoped access token milta hai — password kabhi nahi

Yaad rakhna: Authentication = tum kaun ho (session/JWT/SSO). Authorization = tum kya kar sakte ho (OAuth scopes, permissions). Dono alag hain!

4. Try karo — ek login se teen apps kholo

Google se login karo aur dekho SSO kaise kaam karta hai — phir ek third-party app ko Drive access do aur dekho OAuth token kya-kya kar sakta hai.

5. Paanchon ka comparison table

ConceptKaamKahan rehta hai?Example
SessionLogin state yaad rakhnaServer peWebsite login, Redis session
TokenAccess ka sabootClient peAPI access token
JWTToken ka ek formatClient pe (signed)Authorization: Bearer eyJ...
SSOEk login, kai appsIdP peGoogle se Gmail + Drive + YouTube
OAuthThird-party ko limited accessToken, scoped'Login with Google', Drive access

6. Common galtiyan — ye mat karna

  1. OAuth ko authentication samajhna: OAuth authorization hai (kya kar sakte ho). Login ke liye OIDC chahiye. Sirf OAuth se 'user kaun hai' reliably nahi pata chalta.
  2. SSO ko single point of failure bhoolna: IdP down hua to saari apps band. IdP pe MFA aur backup login zaroor rakho.
  3. JWT ko session ki tarah use karna: JWT me 'logout = token delete' kaam nahi karta — server ko pata hi nahi chalta. Short expiry + refresh token use karo.
  4. Access token ko hamesha ke liye dena: Token ki expiry honi chahiye aur scope limited — 'sab kuch, hamesha ke liye' matlab leak hote hi sab gaya.
  5. Session aur token ko mix karke confuse hona: Session server pe, token client pe — dono ka revoke aur scale alag hai. Use case dekh ke chuno.

7. Interview corner

Q: SSO aur OAuth me farq kya hai?

SSO ek user ko ek login se kai apps me entry deta hai (authentication — 'tum kaun ho'). OAuth ek app ko user ke data tak limited access deta hai (authorization — 'ye app kya kar sakti hai'). SSO ke peeche aksar OAuth/OIDC hi chalta hai, par purpose alag hai.

Q: JWT kya hai — token hai ya session?

JWT ek token format hai — self-contained, signed, stateless. Session server-side record hai. JWT ko session ki tarah use kar sakte ho, par revoke karna mushkil hai — isliye short expiry zaroori hai.

Q: 'Login with Google' ke peeche kya chalta hai?

OAuth 2.0 + OpenID Connect: app tumhe Google (IdP) pe bhejti hai, tum login + consent dete ho, Google app ko authorization code deta hai, app use badal ke ID token (user ki pehchan) aur access token (API access) leti hai. Password app ko kabhi nahi milta.

8. Quick check

Sawaal 1: SSO ka sabse bada fayda kya hai?

  • Password har app ko dena
  • Ek baar login karo, saari connected apps bina dobara login ke khul jaayein [sahi jawab]
  • Har app ka alag password
  • Internet fast ho jata hai

Sawaal 2: OAuth me third-party app ko kya milta hai?

  • Tumhara password
  • Limited scope aur expiry wala access token [sahi jawab]
  • Tumhara poora account
  • Tumhari fingerprint
Ek line me yaad rakh lo: Session = server ka register; Token/JWT = signed saboot client pe; SSO = ek login, kai apps; OAuth = password diye bina limited permission; Authentication (kaun ho) aur Authorization (kya kar sakte ho) alag hain.
Source:https://github.com/ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/blob/main/data/guides/explaining-sessions-tokens-jwt-sso-and-oauth-in-one-diagram.md

08Security (Part 1)

How to Design a Secure System

Secure system koi ek feature nahi hai — ye design ke har faisle me chhupa hota hai: data kahan store hoga, kaun kya dekh sakta hai, attack hone par kya hoga. Is page me ek secure system design karne ka poora framework hai — threat model se leke incident response tak.

1. Secure system — bank ki suraksha

Ek bank sirf ek bada taala nahi lagata. Uske paas kai layers hain: bahar guard, andar CCTV, tijori ka combination lock, har note ka record, aur chori hone par alarm + police. Ek layer fail ho jaye to doosri pakadti hai.

Secure system design wahi hai — defense in depth: ek layer pe bharosa mat karo. Network, application, data, identity — har layer pe alag protection. Aur sabse pehle ye socho: attacker kya chahta hai, aur kahan se aayega? — isse threat modeling kehte hain.

Security ka pehla sawal: 'Kya protect karna hai?' (assets) — 'Kis se?' (threats) — 'Kitna nuksaan ho sakta hai?' (impact). In teen ke bina koi bhi security design andhere me teer hai.

2. Gehrai me samjho — ek-ek point

Threat modeling — pehle socho, phir banao

Threat modeling matlab system ko attacker ki nazar se dekhna. STRIDE framework se har component ko check karo: Spoofing (nakli pehchan), Tampering (data badalna), Repudiation (inkar — 'maine nahi kiya'), Information disclosure (data leak), Denial of service, Elevation of privilege (aam user admin ban jaye).

Example: Ek payment API — Spoofing: koi aur user banke payment kare? Tampering: amount badal de? Repudiation: payment karke 'maine nahi kiya' kahe? Har sawaal ka jawab ek control hai: authentication, signatures, audit logs, rate limiting.

Threat model design ke shuru me banta hai, end me nahi — kyunki end me badlav mehenga padta hai.

Authentication aur Authorization

Authentication (tum kaun ho): Mazboot password policy + MFA (TOTP/hardware key), passkeys jahan possible. Authorization (tum kya kar sakte ho): Least privilege — har user/service ko sirf utna access jitna zaroori hai, usse ek bit zyada nahi.

Service-to-service: Services bhi ek doosre ko authenticate karein (mTLS ya signed tokens) — 'andar ka network safe hai' maan lena sabse badi galti hai (zero trust: har request verify karo, chahe andar se aaye).

Sahi: Har API pe auth check, har service pe least-privilege IAM role, secrets vault me (code me kabhi nahi).

Data protection — transit aur rest

In transit: Har cheez TLS 1.2+ pe — internal traffic bhi. HSTS lagao taaki browser kabhi HTTP pe na jaye. At rest: Database aur disk encryption (AES-256), sensitive fields (PII, card) alag se encrypt ya tokenize karo.

Key management: Keys ko KMS/vault me rakho, rotate karo, aur code/config me kabhi hardcode mat karo. Key leak hui to encryption bekaar hai.

Data minimization: Jo data chahiye hi nahi, use collect hi mat karo. Har extra field ek liability hai — breach me wo bhi leak hoga.

Monitoring, logging aur incident response

Attack hoga — sawaal sirf 'kab' hai. Isliye detection zaroori hai: central logs (SIEM), anomaly alerts (aadhi raat ko 1000 failed logins?), audit trail (kisne, kab, kya kiya).

Incident response plan pehle se likha hona chahiye: (1) Detect — alert aaya. (2) Contain — compromised service ko isolate karo. (3) Eradicate — root cause nikalo, fix karo. (4) Recover — backup se restore karo. (5) Learn — postmortem likho, dobara na ho.

Backups: Encrypted, tested restore, aur ransomware se bachne ke liye offline/immutable copy bhi rakho. Backup jiska restore test nahi hua, wo backup nahi hai.

3. Secure design ke 10 principles (OWASP + industry)

#PrincipleMatlab
1Least privilegeSirf utna access jitna zaroori hai
2Defense in depthKai layers — ek fail to doosri pakde
3Fail securelyError aaye to deny karo, allow nahi
4Zero trustHar request verify karo, andar wali bhi
5Never trust user inputHar input validate + sanitize karo
6Secure by defaultDefault setting safe ho, unsafe opt-in ho
7Keep it simpleComplexity hi vulnerabilities paida karti hai
8Separation of dutiesEk aadmi akela critical kaam na kar sake
9Complete mediationHar access, har baar check ho
10Security through obscurity nahiChhupana ≠ secure; tested algorithms use karo

4. Try karo — ek payment API ko secure banao

Ek payment API bani hai — par usme 4 kamzoriyan hain. Ek-ek karke attack karo, phir fix lagao aur dekho farq.

5. Security layers — ek table me

LayerThreatControl
NetworkDDoS, port scanFirewall, WAF, rate limiting, CDN
IdentityCredential theftMFA, passkeys, SSO, short-lived tokens
ApplicationSQLi, XSS, CSRFInput validation, parameterized queries, CSP
DataLeak, ransomwareEncryption at rest/transit, tokenization, backups
SecretsKey leakVault/KMS, rotation, no hardcoding
MonitoringUndetected breachSIEM, alerts, audit logs, anomaly detection

6. Common galtiyan — ye mat karna

  1. 'Andar ka network safe hai' maan lena: Zero trust rakho — internal service bhi authenticate kare. Lateral movement se hi bade breaches hote hain.
  2. Security ko end me jodna: Design ke baad security chipkana mehenga aur adhoora hota hai. Threat modeling shuru me karo.
  3. Error messages me zyada batana: 'Password galat hai' vs 'User nahi mila' — attacker ko bata rahe ho kaunsa user exist karta hai. Generic message do.
  4. Logs me sensitive data likhna: Password, token, card number logs me — logs leak hote hain, aur ye compliance violation bhi hai.
  5. Incident response plan ka na hona: Breach ke waqt plan banana bahut der ho chuki hoti hai. Plan pehle se likho aur drill karo.

7. Interview corner

Q: Secure system design karte waqt pehla step kya hai?

Threat modeling: kya protect karna hai (assets), kis se (threats), aur kitna nuksaan ho sakta hai (impact). Uske baad STRIDE jaise framework se har component ke threats nikalo, phir unke controls design karo.

Q: Defense in depth ka matlab kya hai?

Ek layer pe bharosa na karke kai layers lagana — firewall, WAF, auth, encryption, monitoring. Ek layer fail ho jaye to doosri attack ko roke ya pakde. Security ek feature nahi, layers ka combination hai.

Q: Fail securely ka matlab kya hai?

Jab kuch galat ho (error, exception, timeout) to system ko deny karna chahiye, allow nahi. Example: authorization check fail ho jaye to user ko andar jaane do — ye fail-open hai, galat hai. Sahi hai fail-closed: error = access deny.

8. Quick check

Sawaal 1: Threat modeling kab karna chahiye?

  • Release ke baad
  • Design ke shuru me [sahi jawab]
  • Breach ke baad
  • Kabhi nahi

Sawaal 2: Defense in depth ka matlab kya hai?

  • Sirf ek strong firewall lagana
  • Kai security layers lagana taaki ek fail ho to doosri pakde [sahi jawab]
  • Password bahut lamba rakhna
  • Server ko chhupa dena
Ek line me yaad rakh lo: Pehle threat model banao (STRIDE), phir layers lagao — least privilege, zero trust, encryption, monitoring; fail securely; incident response plan pehle se ready rakho.
Source:https://github.com/ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/blob/main/data/guides/how-do-we-design-a-secure-system.md
