09Security (Part 1)

How Digital Signatures Work

Jab tum koi document sign karte ho, to do cheezein sabit hoti hain — ye tumne hi sign kiya hai (authenticity) aur uske baad kuch badla nahi gaya (integrity). Digital signature wahi kaam computer pe karta hai — public-key crypto se. Aur haan, ye encryption nahi hai — iska kaam chhupana nahi, sabit karna hai.

1. Digital signature — wax seal wali kahani

Purane zamane me raja apne letter pe wax seal lagata tha — uski angoothi ka nishan. Letter paane wala seal dekh ke jaan jata tha: 'Ye raja ne hi bheja hai, aur raaste me kisi ne khola nahi — seal tooti nahi hai.'

Digital signature wahi wax seal hai: sender apni private key se document ka ek fingerprint (hash) sign karta hai. Koi bhi sender ki public key se verify kar sakta hai: 'Haan, ye signature isi ki hai, aur document badla nahi gaya.'

Farq samjho: Encryption = data chhupana (sirf key wala padhe). Digital signature = data ki pehchan aur integrity sabit karna (koi bhi verify kar sake). Dono me public-key crypto use hota hai, par purpose ulta hai.

2. Gehrai me samjho — ek-ek point

Step by step — kaise banti hai?

1) Hash banao: Document ka hash nikalo (SHA-256) — ek chhota sa fingerprint. Document me ek comma bhi badla to hash poora badal jayega.

2) Hash ko sign karo: Apni private key se hash ko encrypt (sign) karo — yehi digital signature hai. Private key sirf tumhare paas hai.

3) Bhejo: Document + signature, dono bhej do. Document plain bhi ho sakta hai — signature ka kaam chhupana nahi hai.

4) Verify karo: Paane wala document ka hash dobara nikalta hai, aur signature ko tumhari public key se decrypt karke hash se match karta hai. Match hua to document asli aur unchanged hai.

Kya-kya guarantee milti hai?

1) Authentication: Sirf private key wala hi aisa signature bana sakta hai — to ye sabit hota hai ki document kisne bheja.

2) Integrity: Document me ek bit bhi badla to hash badal jayega, signature match nahi karega — tampering pakdi jayegi.

3) Non-repudiation: Sender baad me ye nahi keh sakta 'maine sign nahi kiya' — kyunki private key sirf uske paas thi. Isliye legal documents aur contracts me digital signature chalti hai.

Sahi: Signature hamesha hash pe banti hai, poore document pe nahi — fast aur secure dono.

Digital signature vs HMAC vs Certificate

HMAC: Shared secret key se banta hai — sender aur receiver dono ke paas wahi key hoti hai. Fast hai, par non-repudiation nahi deta (dono me se koi bhi bana sakta hai). APIs me common hai.

Digital signature: Asymmetric keys — private key sirf sender ke paas, public key sabke paas. Non-repudiation milta hai, par slow hai.

Digital certificate: 'Ye public key sach me Priya ki hai' — ye baat ek trusted authority (CA) apne signature se kehti hai. Bina certificate ke koi bhi 'main Priya hoon' keh ke apni public key de sakta hai. TLS isi liye certificates use karta hai.

Kahan use hoti hai?

1) Software updates: Microsoft/Apple apne updates sign karte hain — tumhara computer verify karta hai ki update asli company ka hai, beech me kisi ne badla nahi.

2) Documents (e-sign): Contracts, Aadhaar e-sign — legal validity hoti hai.

3) Blockchain: Har transaction sender ki private key se sign hota hai — bina signature ke transaction valid nahi.

4) Email (DKIM): Email server apne mails sign karta hai — receiver verify karta hai ki mail asli domain se aaya hai, spam nahi.

5) Code signing: Apps aur drivers sign hote hain — OS bina signature wale ko chalane se mana kar deta hai.

3. Sign vs Verify — code ke saath

# Python — digital signature (RSA + SHA-256)
from cryptography.hazmat.primitives.asymmetric import rsa, padding
from cryptography.hazmat.primitives import hashes

# Sender ke paas: private key (secret), public key (sabko pata)
private_key = rsa.generate_private_key(public_exponent=65537, key_size=2048)
public_key = private_key.public_key()

document = b"Contract: Priya will pay Rs 50000 to Amit"

# SIGN: document ka hash, private key se sign karo
signature = private_key.sign(document,
    padding.PSS(mgf=padding.MGF1(hashes.SHA256()),
                salt_length=padding.PSS.MAX_LENGTH),
    hashes.SHA256())

# VERIFY: koi bhi public key se check kar sakta hai
public_key.verify(signature, document,
    padding.PSS(mgf=padding.MGF1(hashes.SHA256()),
                salt_length=padding.PSS.MAX_LENGTH),
    hashes.SHA256())
# Agar document badla hota to verify() exception deta — tampering pakdi jati!

4. Try karo — sign karo, phir tamper karo

Ek contract sign karo. Phir beech me ek attacker amount badalne ki koshish karta hai — dekho signature use kaise pakadta hai.

5. Signature vs Encryption vs Hash — ek table me

CheezKaamKeyExample
EncryptionData chhupanaReceiver ki public key / shared keyWhatsApp messages
Digital signatureAuthenticity + integritySender ki private keySoftware updates, contracts
HashFingerprint nikaalnaKoi key nahiFile integrity check
HMACIntegrity + auth (shared secret)Shared secretAPI request signing
CertificatePublic key kiski hai, ye sabit karnaCA ki signatureHTTPS (TLS)

6. Common galtiyan — ye mat karna

  1. Signature ko encryption samajhna: Signature data ko chhupata nahi — document plain rehta hai, koi bhi padh sakta hai. Chhupana ho to encrypt bhi karo.
  2. Hash ke bina seedha document sign karna: Bada document sign karna slow aur unsafe hai — hamesha pehle hash nikalo, phir hash sign karo.
  3. Private key ko share karna ya backup na rakhna: Private key leak hui to koi bhi tumhare naam se sign kar sakta hai. Key ko HSM/vault me rakho.
  4. Public key ko bina certificate ke maan lena: Koi bhi apni key ko 'Priya ki key' keh sakta hai. Public key ki pehchan ke liye certificate (CA) chahiye.
  5. Expiry aur revocation bhoolna: Key compromise ho to certificate revoke karna padta hai (CRL/OCSP). Bina revocation ke purani key hamesha valid rehti hai.

7. Interview corner

Q: Digital signature kaise kaam karti hai?

Sender document ka hash nikalta hai aur use apni private key se sign karta hai. Receiver document ka hash dobara nikalta hai aur sender ki public key se signature verify karta hai — match hua to document asli hai aur badla nahi gaya.

Q: Digital signature aur encryption me farq?

Encryption data chhupata hai (confidentiality) — receiver ki public key se lock, private key se unlock. Signature authenticity + integrity sabit karta hai — sender ki private key se sign, public key se verify. Document signature me plain rehta hai.

Q: Non-repudiation ka matlab kya hai?

Sender baad me inkar nahi kar sakta ki usne sign nahi kiya — kyunki signature sirf uski private key se ban sakta tha. Isi liye digital signatures contracts aur legal documents me use hoti hain.

8. Quick check

Sawaal 1: Digital signature banane ke liye kis key ka use hota hai?

  • Receiver ki public key
  • Sender ki private key [sahi jawab]
  • Dono ki shared key
  • Koi key nahi

Sawaal 2: Document me ek letter badal diya jaye to signature ka kya hoga?

  • Phir bhi valid rahegi
  • Verify fail ho jayega — hash badal jayega [sahi jawab]
  • Document encrypt ho jayega
  • Kuch nahi hoga
Ek line me yaad rakh lo: Signature = hash + private key; verify = public key se hash match; ye authenticity + integrity + non-repudiation deta hai, confidentiality nahi; public key ki pehchan ke liye certificate chahiye.
Source:https://github.com/ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/blob/main/data/guides/how-digital-signatures-work.md
← PichhlaHow to Design a Secure SystemAgla →How do we manage sensitive data in a system?
10Security (Part 1)

How do we manage sensitive data in a system?

Har system me kuch data aisa hota hai jise leak hona tabahi hai — passwords, card numbers, Aadhaar, health records, API keys. Sensitive data management ka matlab hai: pehchano kaunsa data sensitive hai, use kam se kam jagah rakho, encrypt karo, aur har access ko track karo.

1. Sensitive data — zeher wali kahani

Socho tumhare ghar me ek zeher ki sheeshi hai. Tum use (1) har kamre me nahi rakhte — ek band almari me, (2) uspe label lagate ho 'ZEHER — haath mat lagao', (3) sirf bade hi use chhoo sakte hain, aur (4) har baar jab koi use nikale to diary me likhte ho.

Sensitive data ke saath wahi 4 kaam hote hain: Classify (pehchano kaunsa data sensitive hai), Minimize (jitna kam rakho, utna behtar), Protect (encrypt + access control), Audit (har access log karo). Jo data tumhare paas hai hi nahi, wo leak bhi nahi ho sakta — ye sabse strong protection hai.

Data minimization: Best security wo hai jo data collect hi na kare. Har field poochne se pehle puchho — 'ye data hume sach me chahiye?'

2. Gehrai me samjho — ek-ek point

Classify — pehchano kaunsa data sensitive hai

Har data ek jaisa nahi hota. Classification levels: Public (blog post — koi nuksaan nahi), Internal (company docs — bahar nahi jaana chahiye), Confidential (user PII — email, phone), Restricted (card numbers, passwords, health data — leak = legal trouble).

Classification se hi pata chalta hai kis data pe kitni protection chahiye. Card number pe tokenization, email pe encryption, blog post pe kuch nahi — ek jaisi protection sab pe lagana paise aur time ki barbaadi hai.

PII kya hai? Personally Identifiable Information — naam, email, phone, Aadhaar, address. PHI (health) aur PCI (card) data pe alag kanoon lagte hain (GDPR, HIPAA, PCI DSS).

Protect — encrypt, tokenize, mask karo

Encryption at rest: Database/disk encrypt karo (AES-256). In transit: Har cheez TLS pe. Field-level: Sensitive fields (Aadhaar, phone) ko alag se encrypt karo — taaki DB leak bhi ho to ye fields na khulein.

Tokenization: Card number ki jagah token store karo (vault me asli). Masking: UI/logs me sirf aakhri 4 digit dikhao (**** **** **** 1234). Support team ko poora number dekhne ki zaroorat nahi.

Secrets: API keys aur passwords kabhi code/config me nahi — vault (HashiCorp Vault, AWS Secrets Manager) me, rotation ke saath.

Access control — kaun dekh sakta hai?

Least privilege: Support agent ko user ka email dekhne ki zaroorat hai, password nahi. Developer ko production DB ka read access bhi nahi (masked data se kaam chalao).

Role-based + audit: Sensitive data ko access karne pe har baar log bane — kisne, kab, kya dekha. Anomaly ho (ek agent ne raat ko 1000 records dekhe) to alert aaye.

Separation: Production data ko dev/test me kabhi mat lao — test ke liye synthetic ya masked data banao. Real user data se test karna sabse common leak hai.

Lifecycle — collect se delete tak

Sensitive data ka poora lifecycle manage karo: Collect (sirf zaroori, consent ke saath) → Store (encrypted, classified) → Use (least privilege, audit) → Share (sirf zaroori, encrypted channel, agreement) → Delete (retention policy — kaam khatam hote hi delete karo).

Retention: Har data type ki expiry honi chahiye — logs 90 din, inactive accounts 1 saal, phir auto-delete. GDPR me 'right to be forgotten' hai — user kahe to uska data poori tarah delete karna padta hai, backups se bhi.

Breach plan: Leak hone par 72 ghante me users aur regulator ko batana padta hai (GDPR). Plan pehle se ready rakho.

3. Sensitive data — technique ka chunav

DataTechniqueKyun
PasswordHash + salt (Argon2/bcrypt)Wapas chahiye hi nahi
Card numberTokenizationSystem me aaye hi na (PCI scope kam)
Aadhaar / phoneField-level encryption (AES-256)DB leak ho to bhi safe
API keys / secretsVault + rotationCode me kabhi nahi
Logs / UI displayMasking (****1234)Jo dekhna nahi chahiye, wo dikhe hi na
BackupsEncrypted + access controlBackup bhi leak ho sakta hai
# Masking ka example — logs me kabhi poora card mat likho
# GALAT: log.info(f"Payment failed for card {card_number}")
# SAHI:  log.info(f"Payment failed for card ****{card_number[-4:]}")

4. Try karo — ek user ka data handle karo

Ek naya user signup karta hai. Uske sensitive data ka poora safar dekho — collect se leke delete tak. Ek galti bhi dhoondho!

5. Regulations — kaunsa kanoon kya kehta hai?

RegulationKis parMain rule
GDPR (Europe)EU users ka dataConsent, right to delete, breach notice 72h
DPDP (India)Indian users ka dataConsent, data minimization, breach notice
PCI DSSCard paymentsCard data ko tokenize/encrypt karo, scope kam rakho
HIPAA (US)Health dataStrict access control + encryption

6. Common galtiyan — ye mat karna

  1. Sensitive data ko logs me likhna: Password ya card number log file me — logs leak hote hain. Masking har jagah lagao.
  2. Production data ko dev/test me use karna: Real user data se test karna sabse common leak hai. Synthetic data banao.
  3. Data ko hamesha ke liye rakhna: Retention policy nahi hone se purana data bhi leak hota hai. Expiry aur auto-delete rakho.
  4. Encryption karke key ko usi server pe rakhna: Taala aur chabhi ek hi jagah — key KMS/vault me rakho, alag jagah.
  5. Classification na karna: Sab data ko ek jaisa treat karna — ya to paise barbaad (sab pe heavy protection) ya risk (sensitive data bina protection ke).

7. Interview corner

Q: Sensitive data manage karne ke 4 steps kya hain?

Classify (kaunsa data sensitive hai), Minimize (jitna kam rakho utna behtar), Protect (encrypt/tokenize/mask + access control), Audit (har access log karo). Aur poora lifecycle — collect se delete tak — manage karo.

Q: Card number store karne ka sahi tareeka kya hai?

Tokenization — asli card number vault me, apne system me sirf token. Isse PCI DSS scope kam hota hai aur breach me card safe rehta hai. Kabhi plain card number store mat karo.

Q: Production data test me kyun nahi use karna chahiye?

Kyunki test environment ki security production jaisi nahi hoti — zyada logon ki access, kam monitoring. Real user data wahan leak ho sakta hai. Synthetic ya masked data use karo.

8. Quick check

Sawaal 1: Sensitive data ki sabse strong protection kaunsi hai?

  • Use collect hi na karna (minimization) [sahi jawab]
  • Use bold font me likhna
  • Use alag folder me rakhna
  • Use compress karna

Sawaal 2: Card number ke liye sabse sahi technique kaunsi hai?

  • Plain text
  • Base64 encoding
  • Tokenization [sahi jawab]
  • Logs me likhna
Ek line me yaad rakh lo: Classify karo, minimize karo (jo chahiye hi nahi, wo collect mat karo), encrypt/tokenize/mask karo, least privilege + audit rakho, aur retention ke baad delete karo.
Source:https://github.com/ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/blob/main/data/guides/how-do-we-manage-sensitive-data-in-a-system.md
← PichhlaHow Digital Signatures WorkAgla →HTTPS, SSL Handshake, and Data Encryption Explained
11Security (Part 1)

HTTPS, SSL Handshake, and Data Encryption Explained

Jab tum https:// wali site kholte ho, to tumhare browser aur server ke beech kya hota hai? Kaise pata chalta hai ki site asli hai, aur beech me koi tumhara password padh nahi sakta? Iska jawab hai TLS handshake — ek chhota sa secret handshake jo har secure connection se pehle hota hai.

1. TLS handshake — secret handshake wali kahani

Bachchon ke liye: Socho tum aur tumhara dost ek secret bhasha me baat karna chahte ho, par aas-paas sab sun rahe hain. Pehle tum ek secret code tay karte ho — haath ke ishaaron se, bina bole. Phir usi code me baat karte ho — sunne wale ko kuch samajh nahi aata.

Badon ke liye: Browser aur server pehle asymmetric crypto se ek shared secret (session key) tay karte hain, phir us session key se symmetric crypto (AES) se saari baat-cheet encrypt karte hain. Pehla hissa slow par safe hai (key exchange), doosra hissa fast hai (bulk data).

Ek line me: Handshake = pehchan verify karo (certificate) + secret key tay karo (key exchange). Uske baad sab kuch us key se encrypt hota hai.

2. Gehrai me samjho — ek-ek point

Step 1 — Hello aur Certificate

1) Client Hello: Browser kehta hai 'Namaste! Main TLS 1.3 support karta hoon, ye mere cipher options hain, aur ye ek random number hai.'

2) Server Hello: Server ek cipher chunta hai, apna random number bhejta hai, aur apna certificate bhejta hai — jisme uski public key aur domain likha hota hai, ek trusted CA ke signature ke saath.

3) Verify: Browser certificate check karta hai: kya ye CA trusted hai? Kya domain match karta hai (tum google.com khol rahe ho, certificate bhi google.com ka hai)? Kya expiry nahi hui? Sab theek ho to aage badho — warna browser warning dikhata hai: 'Ye site safe nahi hai!'

Step 2 — Key Exchange

Ab dono ko ek shared secret banana hai — bina use network pe bheje. TLS 1.3 me Diffie-Hellman (ECDHE) use hota hai: dono apna-apna public value bhejte hain, aur dono taraf same secret ban jata hai — beech me sunne wala secret nahi nikaal sakta.

Is secret se session keys banti hain — ek browser → server ke liye, ek server → browser ke liye. Har connection ki keys alag hoti hain — ek connection hack hua to doosra safe (forward secrecy).

Forward secrecy: ECDHE me har session ki key alag hoti hai. Server ki private key baad me leak bhi ho jaye to purani recorded calls decrypt nahi ho sakti — kyunki unki keys alag thi.

Step 3 — Encrypted baat-cheet

Handshake ke baad saara data AES (symmetric encryption) se encrypt hota hai — fast aur secure. Har message ke saath ek MAC bhi hota hai, taaki beech me koi message badal na sake (integrity).

Ab tum jo bhi type karte ho — password, card number — wo encrypted jata hai. Beech me Wi-Fi wala, ISP, ya koi attacker sirf encrypted kachra dekhta hai.

Par dhyaan: HTTPS sirf raaste ko secure karta hai — server khud tumhara data kaise rakhta hai, wo alag baat hai. HTTPS hone ka matlab ye nahi ki site trustworthy hai — phishing sites bhi HTTPS use karti hain!

HTTP vs HTTPS — farq kya hai?

HTTP: Sab kuch plain text me — password, sab kuch, network pe koi bhi padh sakta hai. HTTPS: HTTP + TLS — encrypted, authenticated, tamper-proof.

Browser me taala (lock icon) matlab connection encrypted hai aur certificate valid hai. Taala nahi hai to browser 'Not Secure' likhta hai.

HSTS: Server kehta hai 'mujhe hamesha HTTPS pe kholo' — browser aage se HTTP try hi nahi karta. Isse downgrade attack rukta hai (attacker tumhe HTTP pe dhakel de).

Sahi: Har site pe HTTPS, HSTS on, TLS 1.2+ minimum, purane versions (SSL 3.0, TLS 1.0) band.

3. TLS 1.3 handshake — timeline

TLS 1.3 (sirf 1 round trip!):

Browser                          Server
   | ---- ClientHello -----------> |
   |    (ciphers + random + key share)
   | <--- ServerHello ------------ |
   |    (cipher + random + key share + certificate)
   | <--- Finished --------------- |
   | ---- Finished --------------> |
   | *** Ab se sab encrypted ***   |
   | <==== AES encrypted data ===> |

TLS 1.2 me 2 round trips lagte the — 1.3 fast bhi hai, secure bhi.
0-RTT: pehle se jaani site se dobara connect hone par
pehla data handshake ke saath hi bheja ja sakta hai (par replay risk hota hai).

Certificate chain: Server ka certificate → Intermediate CA → Root CA (browser me pehle se trusted). Browser poori chain verify karta hai — ek kadi bhi tooti to warning.

4. Try karo — ek HTTPS connection banao

Browser bano: ek site kholo, handshake dekho, phir ek attacker aur ek fake site ko bhi try karo — kya hota hai?

5. HTTPS ke 3 guarantees

GuaranteeMatlabKaise
ConfidentialityKoi beech me padh na sakeAES encryption
IntegrityKoi beech me badal na sakeMAC / AEAD
AuthenticationSite wahi hai jo kehti haiCertificate (CA signed)

Yaad rakhna: HTTPS = HTTP + TLS. Taala matlab connection secure hai — site trustworthy hai, ye guarantee nahi hai. Phishing sites bhi HTTPS use karti hain!

6. Common galtiyan — ye mat karna

  1. Browser warning ko ignore karna: 'Your connection is not private' aaye to aage mat badho — certificate me kuch gadbad hai.
  2. HTTPS ko 'site safe hai' samajhna: Phishing sites bhi free certificate le leti hain. URL aur domain hamesha check karo.
  3. HTTP pe password ya card dalna: Plain text me jata hai — koi bhi padh sakta hai. Kabhi mat karo.
  4. TLS 1.0/1.1 ya SSL chalana: Purane versions me jaani-maani kamzoriyan hain (POODLE, BEAST). Minimum TLS 1.2, behtar 1.3.
  5. HSTS na lagana: Bina HSTS ke attacker pehli visit pe HTTP pe dhakel sakta hai (SSL stripping). HSTS + preload list use karo.

7. Interview corner

Q: TLS handshake me kya hota hai?

Pehle ClientHello/ServerHello se cipher aur version tay hota hai, phir server apna certificate bhejta hai jise browser verify karta hai, phir Diffie-Hellman se shared secret banta hai, aur uske baad saara data AES se encrypt hota hai. TLS 1.3 me ye sirf 1 round trip me hota hai.

Q: Forward secrecy kya hai?

Har session ki encryption key alag hoti hai (ECDHE). Server ki private key baad me leak bhi ho jaye to purani recorded conversations decrypt nahi ho sakti — kyunki unki keys private key se nahi bani thi.

Q: HTTPS hone ka matlab site trustworthy hai?

Nahi — HTTPS sirf connection ko secure karta hai (encryption + site ki pehchan certificate se). Phishing site bhi valid certificate le sakti hai. Trust ke liye domain aur site ko alag se check karo.

8. Quick check

Sawaal 1: TLS handshake ka main kaam kya hai?

  • Website ko fast banana
  • Certificate verify karke shared secret key tay karna [sahi jawab]
  • Password store karna
  • Ads dikhana

Sawaal 2: Forward secrecy ka fayda kya hai?

  • Website fast hoti hai
  • Server ki key leak hone par bhi purani calls decrypt nahi hoti [sahi jawab]
  • Password yaad nahi rakhna padta
  • Certificate sasta milta hai
Ek line me yaad rakh lo: Handshake = certificate verify + key exchange (ECDHE), phir AES se encrypted baat; HTTPS deta hai confidentiality + integrity + authentication; taala ≠ trustworthy site; HSTS lagao.
Source:https://github.com/ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/blob/main/data/guides/https-ssl-handshake-and-data-encryption-explained-to-kids.md
← PichhlaHow do we manage sensitive data in a system?Agla →Cybersecurity 101
12Security (Part 1)

Cybersecurity 101

Cybersecurity ek bada shabd hai — par iske peeche sirf ek sawaal hai: 'Mera data aur system, galat logon se kaise bache?' Is page me poora cybersecurity landscape ek saath: threats, defenses, aur tumhare liye practical checklist — beginner se leke interview tak.

1. Cybersecurity — ek sheher ki suraksha vyavastha

Ek sheher ko surakshit rakhne ke liye sirf ek cheez nahi chahiye: border pe guard (firewall), police (monitoring/SOC), taale (encryption), ID card (authentication), kanoon (policies), aur nagrikon ki samajh (awareness — phishing pe click mat karo).

Cybersecurity wahi hai — log, process aur technology ka combination. Sirf tools kharidne se security nahi milti; logon ko train karna aur process banana utna hi zaroori hai. Sabse kamzor kadi aam taur pe technology nahi, insaan hota hai.

CIA triad — security ke 3 pillars: Confidentiality (data sirf authorized log dekhein), Integrity (data badla na jaye), Availability (system jab chahiye tab chale). Har security decision in teeno ko balance karta hai.

2. Gehrai me samjho — ek-ek point

Threats — dushman kaun hain?

Malware: Virus, ransomware (data lock karke paise maangna), spyware, trojan. Phishing: Fake email/site se password churana — sabse common attack. DDoS: Server ko itni requests bhejna ki wo gir jaye. Insider threat: Andar ka aadmi data chura le. Zero-day: Aisi kamzori jiska fix abhi aaya hi nahi.

Social engineering: Technology ko nahi, insaan ko hack karna — 'Main bank se bol raha hoon, OTP batao.' Isse koi firewall nahi rokta — sirf awareness rokti hai.

Attackers ka motive: paise, data, ya disruption. Tum 'chhote' ho, isse koi farq nahi padta — automated attacks sabko target karte hain.

Defenses — bachao kaise karein?

Prevent: Firewall, antivirus, strong passwords + MFA, patching (updates), least privilege. Detect: Monitoring, SIEM, intrusion detection — attack ko jaldi pakdo. Respond: Incident response plan — attack hone par kya karna hai, pehle se tay ho. Recover: Backups — encrypted, tested, offline copy bhi.

Zero Trust: 'Kisi pe bharosa mat karo, har cheez verify karo' — andar ka network bhi safe nahi mana jata. Har user, har device, har request verify hoti hai.

Defense in depth: Ek layer fail ho to doosri pakde — firewall + MFA + encryption + monitoring, sab saath.

CIA Triad — har decision ka scale

Confidentiality: Data sirf authorized log dekhein — encryption, access control. Integrity: Data badla na jaye — hashes, signatures, version control. Availability: System jab chahiye tab mile — redundancy, backups, DDoS protection.

Teeno me balance chahiye: bahut zyada security (har kaam pe 5 baar OTP) to system use hi nahi hoga — availability aur usability kharab. Bahut kam security to breach hoga.

Example: Hospital me patient data confidential bhi hona chahiye, aur emergency me doctor ko turant available bhi — dono ka balance design me sochna padta hai.

Tumhare liye — personal cybersecurity checklist

1) Password manager + har site ka alag password. 2) Har important account pe MFA (TOTP app, SMS nahi). 3) Software update karte raho — purane version me jaani kamzoriyan hoti hain. 4) Phishing: link pe click karne se pehle URL dekho, attachment mat kholo. 5) Backup: important data ka encrypted backup alag jagah rakho. 6) Public Wi-Fi pe sensitive kaam mat karo — ya VPN use karo.

7) 'Urgent' wale message pe shak karo — bank kabhi OTP nahi maangta. 8) Apne accounts ki breach check karo (haveibeenpwned.com).

3. Attack types — ek table me

AttackKaise hota haiBachao
PhishingFake email/site se password churanaURL check, MFA, awareness training
RansomwareData encrypt karke paise maangnaBackups (offline), patching, email filtering
DDoSServer ko requests se bhar denaCDN, rate limiting, cloud scrubbing
SQL InjectionInput me SQL code bhej ke DB nikaalnaParameterized queries, input validation
XSSMalicious script dusre user ke browser me chalanaOutput encoding, CSP, HttpOnly cookies
Man-in-the-MiddleBeech me baat-cheet sunna/badalnaHTTPS, certificate pinning, VPN
Brute forceBaar-baar password guess karnaRate limiting, lockout, strong passwords

4. Try karo — ek din me 5 attacks roko

Tum ek company ke security guard ho. Ek din me 5 alag attacks aate hain — har ek ko pehchano aur sahi defense lagao.

5. Security domains — ek nazar me

DomainKya karta hai
Network securityFirewall, VPN, IDS/IPS
Application securitySecure coding, SAST/DAST, WAF
Identity & accessMFA, SSO, least privilege
Data securityEncryption, DLP, backups
Cloud securityCloud config, CSPM, shared responsibility
Incident responseSOC, forensics, recovery plan
GovernancePolicies, compliance, training

6. Common galtiyan — ye mat karna

  1. 'Hum chhote hain, hume koi hack nahi karega' sochna: Automated attacks sabko target karte hain — size se koi farq nahi padta.
  2. Updates ko taalna: Har update me security fix hota hai. Purana software sabse aasan target hai.
  3. Ek hi password har jagah: Ek leak = saare accounts gaye. Password manager use karo.
  4. Backup ka restore test na karna: Backup hai, par restore kabhi try nahi kiya — ransomware ke waqt pata chala backup corrupt hai.
  5. Security ko sirf IT team ka kaam samajhna: Phishing pe click koi bhi kar sakta hai — har employee ki training zaroori hai.

7. Interview corner

Q: CIA triad kya hai?

Confidentiality (data sirf authorized log dekhein), Integrity (data badla na jaye), Availability (system jab chahiye tab mile). Har security decision in teeno ka balance hota hai.

Q: Defense in depth ka matlab kya hai?

Ek security layer pe bharosa na karke kai layers lagana — firewall, MFA, encryption, monitoring. Ek layer fail ho jaye to doosri attack ko roke ya pakde.

Q: Sabse common attack kaunsa hai aur use kaise rokein?

Phishing — fake email/site se password churana. Bachao: URL dhyaan se dekho, link pe blindly click mat karo, MFA on rakho (password leak bhi ho to account bacha rahe), aur awareness training.

8. Quick check

Sawaal 1: CIA triad ke teen pillars kaunse hain?

  • Computer, Internet, App
  • Confidentiality, Integrity, Availability [sahi jawab]
  • Code, Info, Access
  • Cloud, IoT, AI

Sawaal 2: Phishing attack se sabse achha bachao kya hai?

  • Antivirus
  • URL dhyaan se dekhna + MFA on rakhna [sahi jawab]
  • Password lamba rakhna
  • Internet band kar dena
Ek line me yaad rakh lo: Cybersecurity = CIA triad (confidentiality, integrity, availability) + defense in depth + log/process/technology; sabse common attack phishing hai — awareness + MFA sabse bada bachao hai.

Cybersecurity frameworks — guide me sirf heading hai, ye standard frameworks hain

Guide ke "Cybersecurity Frameworks" section me sirf heading hai, detail nahi — isliye ye 3 standard frameworks yahan likhe hain, jo interviews me sabse zyada poochhe jate hain:

  • NIST CSF (Cybersecurity Framework): Identify, Protect, Detect, Respond, Recover — 5 functions me security program organize karo.
  • ISO/IEC 27001: information security management system (ISMS) ka international standard — controls ka poora set, audit aur certification ke saath.
  • CIS Controls: 18 prioritized safeguards — sabse pehle basic hygiene (inventory, patching, access control), phir advanced defenses.

Framework ka kaam hai: defense mechanisms ko ek checklist me bandhna, taaki koi cheez chhoot na jaye.

Source:https://github.com/ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/blob/main/data/guides/cybersecurity-101-in-one-picture.md
← PichhlaHTTPS, SSL Handshake, and Data Encryption ExplainedAgla →Cookies vs Sessions vs JWT vs PASETO
13Security (Part 1)

Cookies vs Sessions vs JWT vs PASETO

Login ke baad user ko pehchanne ke 4 tareeke — Cookie, Session, JWT aur naya PASETO. JWT ke baare me to sab jaante hain, par PASETO kya hai aur wo JWT se behtar kyun kaha jata hai? Is page me chaaron ka fair comparison hai.

1. Chaaron ko ek kahani se samjho — club entry

Session: Club ke register me tumhara naam — entry pe guard register dekhta hai. Cookie: Tumhare haath ka stamp — guard stamp dekh ke jaane deta hai (stamp khud kuch nahi kehta, register kehta hai). JWT: Tumhare haath ka card — naam, expiry, aur club ki mohar sab likhi hai; guard card padh ke jaane deta hai, register nahi dekhta. PASETO: Wahi card, par uska design aisa hai ki mohar galat tareeke se lag hi nahi sakti — card banane wale se galti hone ka chance hi nahi.

Farq samjho: JWT ek standard hai jisme galat choices possible hain (kamzor algorithm chun lo to hack ho jayega). PASETO ek opinionated design hai — galat choice karne ka option hi nahi diya gaya.

Ek line me: Cookie = carrier, Session = server yaad rakhta hai, JWT = signed token (flexible par galti possible), PASETO = signed/encrypted token (safe by default).

2. Gehrai me samjho — ek-ek point

Cookie aur Session — recap

Cookie browser storage hai — server Set-Cookie se data deta hai, browser har request me wapas bhejta hai. Session server-side record hai — browser me sirf session ID (cookie me) rehta hai.

Dono saath kaam karte hain: session ID cookie me travel karti hai. Plus: Revoke turant, data server pe safe. Minus: Server ko state rakhni padti hai, scale ke liye shared store chahiye.

Traditional web apps ke liye aaj bhi best choice hai — simple aur control tumhare haath me.

JWT — popular, par galti ki gunjaish

JWT stateless token hai — Header.Payload.Signature. Server ko lookup nahi karna padta, microservices me popular hai.

Par JWT me footguns hain: (1) Algorithm confusion — attacker alg: none bhej de. (2) RS256 → HS256 confusion — public key ko HMAC secret maan liya jaye. (3) Payload me sensitive data — koi bhi decode kar sakta hai. (4) Expiry bhool jana — lifetime token. (5) Weak secret — 'secret123' se sign karna.

Ye saari galtiyan developer ki hain, JWT ki nahi — par standard ne in galtiyon ka raasta khula chhoda hai.

PASETO — JWT ka safe version

PASETO (Platform-Agnostic Security Tokens) 2018 me bana — JWT ki kamiyon ko fix karne ke liye. Iske do versions: v2.local (symmetric — encrypted, sirf key wala padh sakta hai) aur v2.public (asymmetric — signed, koi bhi verify kar sakta hai).

Kya behtar hai: (1) Algorithm fixed hai — version se hi pata chalta hai kaunsa crypto use hoga, chunne ka option hi nahi. (2) alg: none possible hi nahi. (3) Local tokens encrypted hote hain — payload koi nahi padh sakta. (4) Har token me expiry aur footer ka standard format hai.

Kami: Ecosystem chhota hai — JWT ki tarah har library/framework me support nahi hai. Isliye adoption dheere hai.

Kaunsa kab? — decision guide

Web app (server-rendered): Session + Cookie — simple, revoke aasan.

API / mobile / microservices: JWT (sahi tareeke se — short expiry, strong key, algorithm whitelist) ya PASETO (agar libraries available hon).

Naya project, security-first: PASETO try karo — safe defaults ki wajah se galti kam hogi.

Existing JWT system: PASETO me migrate karne ki jaldi nahi — JWT ko sahi rules se use karo (short expiry, refresh token, strong keys) to wo bhi safe hai.

Interview line: 'JWT bura nahi hai — uske defaults bura hain. PASETO ne wahi defaults fix kiye hain.'

3. Chaaron ka comparison

CheezCookieSessionJWTPASETO
Kya hai?Browser storageServer-side recordSigned tokenSigned/encrypted token
Stateful?—HaanNahiNahi
Payload dikhta hai?Haan (JS bhi, agar HttpOnly nahi)Nahi (server pe)Haan (Base64)Local: Nahi (encrypted)
RevokeDelete karkeTurantMushkilMushkil
Galti ki gunjaishFlags bhoolnaKamZyada (alg, expiry, secret)Kam (fixed algorithms)
EcosystemUniversalUniversalHar jagahBadhta hua
# PASETO v2.local — payload ENCRYPTED hota hai (JWT se farq!)
# Token format: v2.local.
# v2.public — signed hota hai (JWT jaisa, par algorithm fixed)
# Dono me version se hi pata chalta hai kaunsa crypto — koi choice nahi, koi confusion nahi

4. Try karo — JWT attack vs PASETO

Ek attacker JWT ke jaane-maane attacks try karta hai. Dekho kaunsa attack JWT pe chalta hai aur PASETO pe kyun nahi.

5. PASETO ke versions

VersionTypeKaam
v2.localSymmetric (encrypted)Sirf key wala padh aur verify kar sakta hai — internal services
v2.publicAsymmetric (signed)Koi bhi verify kar sakta hai, sirf key wala bana sakta hai — public APIs
v4.local / v4.publicNewer cryptov2 ka updated version, behtar algorithms

Rule: Local = secret (encrypted), Public = signed (verify sab kar sakte hain). Naam se hi pata chalta hai — JWT me ye confusion hoti thi.

6. Common galtiyan — ye mat karna

  1. JWT ko 'encrypted' samajhna: JWT signed hota hai, encrypted nahi — payload koi bhi padh sakta hai. Confidentiality chahiye to JWE ya PASETO local use karo.
  2. Algorithm ko token se lene dena: Server hamesha apna expected algorithm enforce kare — warna alg=none ya RS256→HS256 confusion attack hoga.
  3. PASETO ko 'JWT ka replacement' maan ke bina soche migrate karna: Ecosystem aur library support check karo — agar tumhare stack me PASETO library nahi hai to JWT ko sahi tareeke se use karna behtar hai.
  4. Session aur token ko ek hi samajhna: Session revoke turant hota hai, token nahi — use case dekh ke chuno.
  5. Cookie flags bhoolna: Chahe session ID ho ya JWT, cookie me rakh rahe ho to HttpOnly + Secure + SameSite lagao.

7. Interview corner

Q: PASETO JWT se behtar kyun kaha jata hai?

Kyunki PASETO me algorithms fixed hain — version se hi pata chalta hai kaunsa crypto use hoga. alg=none ya algorithm confusion attack possible hi nahi. Aur v2.local tokens encrypted hote hain, to payload koi nahi padh sakta. JWT me ye saari galtiyan developer kar sakta hai.

Q: JWT ka sabse bada security risk kya hai?

Algorithm confusion aur weak secrets — alg=none attack, RS256 public key ko HS256 secret maan lena, aur kamzor secret se sign karna. Fix: algorithm whitelist, strong random keys, short expiry.

Q: Cookie, Session, JWT, PASETO — ek line me farq?

Cookie ek storage/transport mechanism hai; Session server-side record hai (revoke turant); JWT stateless signed token hai (flexible par galti possible); PASETO stateless token hai jo safe defaults ke saath aata hai.

8. Quick check

Sawaal 1: PASETO JWT se safe kyun hai?

  • Ye fast hai
  • Isme algorithm fixed hai — galat choice ka option hi nahi, aur local tokens encrypted hote hain [sahi jawab]
  • Isme password nahi hota
  • Ye bada hota hai

Sawaal 2: JWT ka payload kyun sensitive data ke liye safe nahi hai?

  • Payload encrypt hota hai
  • Payload sirf Base64 hai — koi bhi decode karke padh sakta hai [sahi jawab]
  • Payload bahut chhota hota hai
  • Payload server pe rehta hai
Ek line me yaad rakh lo: Cookie = carrier; Session = server pe, revoke turant; JWT = stateless, popular par galti ki gunjaish (alg, expiry, secret); PASETO = safe-by-default token, fixed algorithms + encrypted local tokens.
Source:https://github.com/ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/blob/main/data/guides/cookies-vs-sessions-vs-jwt-vs-paseto.md
← PichhlaCybersecurity 101Agla →How does SSH work?
14Security (Part 1)

How does SSH work?

Jab tum ssh user@server likhte ho aur ek remote computer ka terminal khul jata hai — peeche kya hota hai? SSH (Secure Shell) ek encrypted tunnel banata hai, server ki pehchan verify karta hai, aur tumhe securely login karata hai. Telnet ka secure replacement — jo aaj bhi har server ka lifeline hai.

1. SSH — secret tunnel wali kahani

Socho tum ek building ke andar jaana chahte ho. Pehle tum gate pe guard se milte ho — wo apna ID card dikhata hai (server apna host key dikhata hai, tum verify karte ho 'ye wahi server hai?'). Phir tum dono mil ke ek secret tunnel banate ho (encrypted connection) — uske andar jo bhi baat hogi, bahar koi nahi sun sakta. Phir tum apni pehchan dikhate ho — password ya apni chabhi (SSH key) — aur andar jaate ho.

Telnet me ye tunnel nahi tha — password plain text me jata tha, koi bhi padh sakta tha. SSH ne wahi kaam encrypted kar diya, aur aaj SSH sirf terminal ke liye nahi — file transfer (SCP/SFTP), port forwarding, aur Git ke liye bhi use hota hai.

Ek line me: SSH = server verify karo + encrypted tunnel banao + key/password se login karo. Teen steps, har baar.

2. Gehrai me samjho — ek-ek point

Step 1 — Server ki pehchan (host key)

Connect karte hi server apni host key (public key) bhejta hai. Tumhara SSH client check karta hai: kya ye key pehle se jaani hai (~/.ssh/known_hosts me)? Pehli baar ho to poochta hai: 'Is key pe bharosa karoon?'

$ ssh user@192.168.1.10
The authenticity of host '192.168.1.10' can't be established.
ED25519 key fingerprint is SHA256:abc123...
Are you sure you want to continue connecting (yes/no)?

Ye step man-in-the-middle se bachata hai — agar koi fake server beech me aa jaye to uski key alag hogi, aur client warning dega: 'WARNING: REMOTE HOST IDENTIFICATION HAS CHANGED!'

Galat: Fingerprint check kiye bina blindly 'yes' kar dena — pehli baar hi sahi, par fingerprint ko alag channel se verify karna chahiye.

Step 2 — Encrypted tunnel (key exchange)

Server verify hone ke baad dono Diffie-Hellman key exchange se ek shared secret banate hain — bina use network pe bheje. Us secret se symmetric session key banti hai (AES/ChaCha20), aur uske baad saara data encrypt hota hai.

Ye TLS handshake jaisa hi hai — farq sirf itna hai ki SSH certificates (CA) use nahi karta, seedha host keys use karta hai. Har session ki key alag hoti hai (forward secrecy).

Is tunnel ke andar ab kuch bhi safe hai — commands, passwords, files — sab encrypted.

Step 3 — Login (password vs SSH key)

Password auth: Tum password type karte ho — encrypted tunnel ke andar jata hai, server check karta hai. Simple hai, par brute-force ho sakta hai — isliye production servers pe password auth band karke sirf key auth rakhte hain.

Public key auth (behtar): Tumhare paas key pair hai — private key tumhare laptop pe (~/.ssh/id_ed25519), public key server pe (~/.ssh/authorized_keys me). Server ek challenge bhejta hai, tumhari private key use sign karti hai, server public key se verify karta hai — password type hi nahi karna padta, aur brute-force impossible hai.

# Key pair banao (ek baar)
ssh-keygen -t ed25519 -C "priya@laptop"
# Public key server pe daalo
ssh-copy-id user@server
# Ab se: ssh user@server → bina password ke login ✓

SSH ke aur kaam — sirf terminal nahi

SCP/SFTP: Files securely bhejo — scp file.txt user@server:/tmp/. Port forwarding: Remote service ko local port pe lao — ssh -L 8080:localhost:80 user@server se remote ka port 80 tumhare laptop ke 8080 pe dikhega.

Git over SSH: git@github.com:user/repo.git — har push/pull SSH se authenticate hota hai. SSH tunneling: Kisi bhi traffic ko SSH ke andar se bhej do — ek tarah ka personal VPN.

ssh-agent: Private key ko ek baar unlock karo, phir har connection pe dobara passphrase nahi mangta — secure bhi, convenient bhi.

3. Poora flow — ek diagram ki tarah

Client (tumhara laptop)                  Server
   | ---- "ssh user@server" ------------> |
   | <--- Host key (public) ------------- |
   |      (known_hosts se verify karo)    |
   | ---- Key exchange ----------------> |
   | <--- Shared secret tay hua --------- |
   | *** Encrypted tunnel ban gaya ***    |
   | ---- Auth: challenge sign karo ----> |
   |      (private key se)               |
   | <--- Verify OK, welcome! ----------- |
   | <==== Encrypted terminal session ===> |
   |      commands, output, files...      |

Server hardening checklist: Password auth band karo (PasswordAuthentication no), root login band karo (PermitRootLogin no), default port 22 badlo ya fail2ban lagao, sirf key auth allow karo, aur authorized_keys ko regularly audit karo.

4. Try karo — SSH se server me ghuso

Ek server se connect karo: pehle host key verify karo, phir password se login karo, phir key-based login try karo — aur ek attacker ko bhi dekho.

5. SSH vs Telnet vs FTP — kyun SSH jeetta hai?

ProtocolEncryptionUseStatus
Telnet❌ Nahi — sab plain textRemote terminal❌ Band karo — password sab padh sakte hain
FTP❌ NahiFile transfer❌ SFTP use karo
SSH✅ HaanTerminal + files + forwarding✅ Standard
SFTP/SCP✅ SSH ke andarFile transfer✅ Standard

6. Common galtiyan — ye mat karna

  1. Password auth ko production pe on rakhna: Brute-force bots din-raat try karte hain. Sirf key auth rakho, password band karo.
  2. Private key ko share ya upload karna: Private key sirf tumhare paas — GitHub, email ya chat pe kabhi mat bhejo. Leak hui to turant nayi key banao.
  3. Host key warning ignore karna: 'REMOTE HOST IDENTIFICATION HAS CHANGED' aaye to aage mat badho — ya to server reinstall hua hai, ya MITM attack hai.
  4. Root login allow karna: Root se seedha SSH matlab attacker ko sabse powerful account mil gaya. Normal user se login karo, phir sudo karo.
  5. Private key bina passphrase ke rakhna: Laptop chori hua to key bhi gayi. Passphrase lagao + ssh-agent use karo.

7. Interview corner

Q: SSH kaise kaam karta hai?

Teen steps: (1) Server apni host key bhejta hai, client known_hosts se verify karta hai. (2) Diffie-Hellman key exchange se encrypted tunnel banta hai. (3) User password ya public-key auth se login karta hai — private key challenge sign karti hai, server public key se verify karta hai.

Q: SSH key auth password se behtar kyun hai?

Kyunki password brute-force ho sakta hai aur phish bhi ho sakta hai; private key ko guess nahi kiya ja sakta, wo kabhi network pe nahi jati (sirf challenge sign hota hai), aur password type hi nahi karna padta.

Q: Host key kis kaam aati hai?

Server ki pehchan verify karne ke — taaki man-in-the-middle attack na ho. Pehli baar connect karte waqt key save hoti hai; baad me key badli to client warning deta hai.

8. Quick check

Sawaal 1: SSH me server ki pehchan kaise verify hoti hai?

  • Password se
  • Host key se — known_hosts se match karke [sahi jawab]
  • Username se
  • IP address se

Sawaal 2: Public key auth me private key kahan rehti hai?

  • Server pe
  • Tumhare laptop pe — kabhi network pe nahi jati [sahi jawab]
  • GitHub pe
  • Email me
Ek line me yaad rakh lo: SSH = host key verify + encrypted tunnel + key/password login; password auth band karke key auth use karo; private key kabhi share mat karo; host key warning ko ignore mat karo.

SSH ki 3 layers — poora protocol 3 hisson me

SSH ke 2 versions hain — SSH-1 aur SSH-2; SSH-2 ko IETF ne standardize kiya hai. Protocol ki 3 main layers hain:

  • Transport Layer: encryption, integrity aur data protection deti hai — client aur server ke beech secure communication ki buniyaad hai.
  • Authentication Layer: client ki identity verify karti hai — sirf authorized users hi server access kar sakein.
  • Connection Layer: encrypted aur authenticated communication ko multiple logical channels me multiplex karti hai — ek hi connection par terminal, file transfer aur port forwarding ek saath chal sakte hain.
Source:https://github.com/ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/blob/main/data/guides/how-does-ssh-work.md
← PichhlaCookies vs Sessions vs JWT vs PASETOAgla →How Does a VPN Work?
15Security (Part 1)

How Does a VPN Work?

Public Wi-Fi pe baithe ho aur bank login kar rahe ho — koi beech me tumhara data padh sakta hai? VPN (Virtual Private Network) tumhare aur internet ke beech ek encrypted tunnel banata hai: tumhara data pehle VPN server tak encrypted jata hai, phir wahan se internet pe. Par VPN kya-kya bachata hai, aur kya nahi — ye samajhna zaroori hai.

1. VPN — private courier wali kahani

Socho tum ek letter bhej rahe ho. Bina VPN ke tum use khule postcard ki tarah bhej rahe ho — postman, padosi, koi bhi padh sakta hai. VPN ke saath tum letter ko ek band box me daal ke ek bharosemand courier (VPN server) ko dete ho. Courier box ko khol ke letter ko aage bhejta hai. Raaste me koi box ke andar nahi dekh sakta.

Par dhyaan do: courier ko letter dikhta hai! Isliye VPN provider pe bharosa zaroori hai — wo tumhara data dekh sakta hai, log kar sakta hai, bech bhi sakta hai. Isi liye 'free VPN' sabse khatarnak hota hai — tum product nahi, to tumhara data hi product hai.

Ek line me: VPN = tumhara traffic pehle VPN server tak encrypted jata hai, phir wahan se internet pe. Wi-Fi wala aur ISP tumhara data nahi dekh sakte — par VPN provider dekh sakta hai.

2. Gehrai me samjho — ek-ek point

Tunnel kaise banta hai?

1) Tum VPN app kholte ho, server chunte ho (jaise Mumbai server). 2) Tumhara device aur VPN server ke beech encrypted tunnel banta hai — protocols: OpenVPN, WireGuard (naya, fast), IKEv2/IPsec. Handshake me keys exchange hoti hain (TLS jaisi). 3) Ab tumhara saara internet traffic pehle is tunnel se VPN server tak jata hai, phir server use internet pe bhejta hai.

Website ko tumhara asli IP nahi, VPN server ka IP dikhta hai. Tum Mumbai server se jude ho to site ko lagega tum Mumbai me ho — geo-blocked content khul jata hai.

VPN kya bachata hai?

1) Public Wi-Fi pe safety: Cafe/airport Wi-Fi pe attacker tumhara data nahi padh sakta — sab encrypted hai. 2) ISP se privacy: ISP ko nahi pata tum kaunsi sites khol rahe ho — sirf ye pata hai tum VPN se jude ho. 3) Geo-restriction: Doosre desh ka content dekh sakte ho. 4) Office access: Ghar se office network securely — corporate VPN.

Kill switch: Agar VPN connection toot jaye to internet bhi band ho jata hai — taaki tumhara data bina encryption ke leak na ho. Achhe VPN me ye hona chahiye.

VPN kya NAHI bachata?

1) VPN provider se nahi: Provider tumhara traffic dekh sakta hai — no-log policy wala trusted provider chuno. 2) Malware/phishing se nahi: Fake site pe jaoge to VPN bhi nahi bacha sakta. 3) Tracking se poori tarah nahi: Google/Facebook tumhe cookies aur login se pehchan lete hain — VPN IP badalne se ye nahi rukta. 4) Anonymity nahi deta: VPN privacy deta hai, anonymity nahi — Tor alag cheez hai (multiple hops, koi ek node poora raasta nahi jaanta).

DNS leak: Agar DNS queries VPN tunnel se bahar jaayein to ISP ko pata chal jayega tum kahan gaye. Achha VPN DNS leak protection deta hai.

VPN protocols — kaunsa kab?

WireGuard: Naya, fast, simple code (4000 lines) — aaj ka best choice. OpenVPN: Purana, battle-tested, har jagah support — thoda slow. IKEv2/IPsec: Mobile pe achha (network badalne par reconnect fast). PPTP: Purana aur toota hua — kabhi mat use karo.

Corporate VPN vs Commercial VPN: Corporate VPN tumhe office network se jodta hai (kaam ke liye). Commercial VPN (NordVPN, ProtonVPN) tumhe internet pe privacy deta hai. Dono ka kaam alag hai.

3. VPN on vs off — kya dikhta hai kisko?

KaunVPN OFF — kya dekhta haiVPN ON — kya dekhta hai
Wi-Fi attackerTumhari sites, passwords (HTTP pe)Sirf encrypted kachra
ISPHar site jo tum kholte hoSirf 'VPN se juda hai'
WebsiteTumhara asli IP + locationVPN server ka IP + location
VPN providerKuch nahiTumhara traffic (bharosa zaroori!)

Split tunneling: Kuch apps VPN se, kuch seedha internet se — jaise banking app seedha, baaki sab VPN se. Battery aur speed bachti hai, par dhyaan se configure karo.

4. Try karo — VPN on karo, phir test karo

Cafe ki public Wi-Fi pe baithe ho. Pehle bina VPN ke, phir VPN ke saath — dekho attacker, ISP aur website ko kya dikhta hai.

5. VPN vs Tor vs Proxy — farq

CheezVPNTorProxy
Encryption✅ Poora traffic✅ Multiple layers⚠ Aksar nahi
SpeedFastSlowFast
AnonymityPartialStrongNahi
Provider trustChahiyeKam (distributed)Chahiye
Best forWi-Fi safety, geo-contentHigh anonymitySimple IP change

6. Common galtiyan — ye mat karna

  1. Free VPN use karna: Free VPN tumhara data bech ke paise kamata hai. Trusted provider chuno, no-log policy check karo.
  2. VPN ko anonymity samajhna: VPN privacy deta hai, anonymity nahi. Login karke Google use karoge to Google tumhe pehchan lega.
  3. Kill switch off rakhna: VPN toote to traffic leak ho jata hai. Kill switch hamesha on rakho.
  4. VPN pe phishing se safe samajhna: VPN fake site ko asli nahi banata. URL aur domain abhi bhi check karo.
  5. Corporate VPN se personal kaam karna: Office VPN pe tumhara traffic company dekh sakti hai. Personal kaam personal network/VPN se karo.

7. Interview corner

Q: VPN kaise kaam karta hai?

VPN tumhare device aur VPN server ke beech ek encrypted tunnel banata hai. Tumhara saara traffic pehle tunnel se server tak jata hai, phir server use internet pe bhejta hai. Isse Wi-Fi attacker aur ISP tumhara data nahi dekh sakte, aur website ko VPN server ka IP dikhta hai.

Q: VPN kya protect nahi karta?

VPN provider khud tumhara traffic dekh sakta hai — isliye trusted provider zaroori hai. VPN malware, phishing ya tracking (cookies/login) se nahi bachata. Aur ye anonymity nahi deta — Tor alag cheez hai.

Q: WireGuard OpenVPN se behtar kyun kaha jata hai?

WireGuard ka code bahut chhota aur simple hai (~4000 lines vs OpenVPN ke lakhon), isliye audit karna aasan aur attack surface kam hai. Ye fast bhi hai aur mobile pe network badalne par jaldi reconnect karta hai.

8. Quick check

Sawaal 1: VPN on hone par website ko kya dikhta hai?

  • Tumhara asli IP
  • VPN server ka IP [sahi jawab]
  • Tumhara password
  • Kuch nahi

Sawaal 2: Free VPN khatarnak kyun ho sakta hai?

  • Ye slow hota hai
  • Ye tumhara data log karke/bech ke paise kamata hai [sahi jawab]
  • Ye sirf ek desh me chalta hai
  • Isme password nahi hota
Ek line me yaad rakh lo: VPN = device se server tak encrypted tunnel; Wi-Fi aur ISP se bachata hai, provider se nahi; kill switch on rakho; free VPN se bacho; phishing/malware se VPN nahi bachata.

VPN ke fayde aur nuksaan — ek table me

FaydeKaise
PrivacyISP aur network wale tumhari activity nahi dekh sakte
AnonymityAsli IP chhup jata hai, VPN server ka IP dikhta hai
SecurityPublic Wi-Fi par bhi data encrypted rehta hai
EncryptionSaara traffic tunnel ke andar encrypted jata hai
Masking the original IP addressWebsite ko lagta hai request VPN server se aa rahi hai
NuksaanKaise
VPN blockingKuch sites aur networks VPN traffic ko block kar dete hain
Slow down connectionsEncryption + extra hop ki wajah se speed kam ho jati hai
Trust in VPN providerVPN provider tumhara saara traffic dekh sakta hai — galat provider matlab privacy ka koi fayda nahi
Source:https://github.com/ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/blob/main/data/guides/how-does-a-vpn-work.md
← PichhlaHow does SSH work?Agla →How Google Authenticator Works
16Security (Part 1)

How Google Authenticator Works

Login karte waqt 6-digit code maanga jata hai jo har 30 second me badal jata hai — aur ye code bina internet ke bhi banta hai! Google Authenticator jaisi TOTP apps kaise kaam karti hain? Iska raaz hai ek shared secret aur time — is page me poora mechanism samjho.

1. TOTP — ghadi wala taala

Socho tumhare aur bank ke paas ek hi ghadi hai, aur ek hi secret formula hai. Har 30 second me tum dono formula + current time se ek naya number banate ho. Bank tumse number poochta hai — tumhara number uske number se match hua to tum wahi ho.

Internet ki zaroorat nahi — kyunki dono ke paas ghadi hai aur formula hai. Attacker ko number chahiye to use ya to tumhara phone chahiye, ya secret formula — dono me se ek bhi nahi milta aasan se.

Ek line me: TOTP = shared secret + current time → 6-digit code. Server aur phone dono ek hi code banate hain — match hua to login.

2. Gehrai me samjho — ek-ek point

Setup — secret kaise share hota hai?

1) Site pe 2FA on karte ho — site ek random secret key banati hai (jaise JBSWY3DPEHPK3PXP). 2) Site use QR code me dikhati hai. 3) Tum Authenticator app se QR scan karte ho — secret tumhare phone me save ho jata hai. 4) Site secret ko tumhare account se jod ke apne server pe store karti hai.

QR code ek baar scan karne ke baad secret phone me rehta hai — dobara internet ki zaroorat nahi. Backup codes bhi milte hain — phone kho jaye to unse login kar sakte ho. Inhe safe jagah rakho!

Galat: QR code ka screenshot leke kisi ko bhej dena — usme secret hai, koi bhi tumhare codes bana sakta hai.

Code kaise banta hai? — TOTP algorithm

TOTP (Time-based One-Time Password, RFC 6238) ka formula simple hai:

counter = current Unix time / 30  (har 30 sec me naya counter)
code = HMAC-SHA1(secret, counter)  → usme se 6 digit nikaalo

Example:
Time: 12:00:00 → counter 55555555 → code 482 917
Time: 12:00:30 → counter 55555556 → code 731 204  (badal gaya!)

Server bhi wahi formula chalata hai — uske paas bhi secret hai aur time hai. Tumhara code uske code se match hua to login. Time me thoda farq ho to server ek step aage-peeche bhi check karta hai (clock skew ke liye).

HOTP vs TOTP: HOTP counter-based hai (har use pe counter badhta hai — purane hardware tokens). TOTP time-based hai — aaj ka standard.

TOTP vs SMS OTP — farq kya hai?

SMS OTP: Code SMS se aata hai — network pe travel karta hai. SIM swap attack se attacker tumhara number apne phone pe le sakta hai aur OTP padh sakta hai. SS7 flaws se bhi intercept ho sakta hai.

TOTP: Code tumhare phone me locally banta hai — network pe kuch nahi aata. SIM swap se koi farq nahi padta. Offline bhi kaam karta hai (flight mode me bhi!).

Isliye security experts kehte hain: SMS 2FA se TOTP 2FA behtar hai. Aur sabse behtar hai hardware security key (FIDO2) — jo phishing-proof bhi hai.

Phone kho gaya to kya hoga?

1) Backup codes: Setup ke waqt mile the — unse login karo, phir 2FA dobara set karo. 2) Recovery: Kuch sites backup email ya ID verification se 2FA reset karti hain. 3) Cloud backup: Authy ya Google Authenticator ka cloud sync on ho to naye phone pe codes wapas mil jate hain (encrypted sync).

Lesson: 2FA on karte hi backup codes ko safe jagah (password manager ya printed copy) rakho. Phone kho gaya aur backup nahi — to account recover karna dinon ka kaam ho sakta hai.

Sahi: Backup codes ko password manager me save karo — wahi jagah jahan master password hai.

3. 2FA methods ka comparison

MethodSecurityPhishing-proof?Offline?
SMS OTP⚠ Kamzor (SIM swap)❌ Nahi❌ Network chahiye
TOTP app (Authenticator)✅ Achha⚠ Partial (code phish ho sakta hai)✅ Haan
Push notification✅ Achha⚠ Partial (MFA fatigue attack)❌ Network chahiye
Hardware key (YubiKey)✅✅ Best✅ Haan✅ Haan
Passkey✅✅ Best✅ Haan✅ Haan

MFA fatigue attack: Attacker baar-baar push notification bhejta hai, user pareshan hoke 'Approve' daba deta hai. Bachao: number matching (app pe dikha number type karo) ya hardware key use karo.

4. Try karo — TOTP code banao aur login karo

Ek TOTP app bano: secret aur time se code banao, phir login karo. Phir dekho SIM swap aur phishing se TOTP kaise bachta hai.

5. TOTP ke baare me zaroori facts

CheezFact
StandardRFC 6238 (TOTP), RFC 4226 (HOTP)
Code validity30 second (aam taur pe)
Secret shareEk baar QR se — dobara nahi
InternetCode banane ke liye nahi chahiye
Server kya store karta haiSecret key (encrypted honi chahiye)
Clock syncPhone aur server ka time sync hona chahiye

6. Common galtiyan — ye mat karna

  1. SMS OTP ko kaafi samajhna: SIM swap se SMS OTP chori ho jata hai. TOTP app ya hardware key use karo.
  2. Backup codes ko save na karna: Phone kho gaya aur backup nahi — account lock. Setup karte hi backup codes save karo.
  3. QR code ka screenshot share karna: QR me secret hota hai — screenshot kisi ko bheja to wo bhi tumhare codes bana sakta hai.
  4. 2FA ko sirf login pe lagana: Sensitive actions (password change, paise transfer) pe bhi dobara code maango.
  5. Push notification ko blindly approve karna: MFA fatigue attack — achanak aaye approve request ko hamesha verify karo, blindly mat dabao.

7. Interview corner

Q: Google Authenticator bina internet ke code kaise banata hai?

Kyunki code internet se nahi aata — wo phone me locally banta hai. Phone aur server dono ke paas ek shared secret hai aur dono ke paas time hai. TOTP algorithm (HMAC-SHA1 of secret + time/30) se dono ek hi 6-digit code banate hain. Match hua to login.

Q: TOTP SMS OTP se behtar kyun hai?

SMS OTP network se aata hai — SIM swap attack se attacker tumhara number leke OTP padh sakta hai. TOTP code phone me locally banta hai, network pe kuch travel nahi karta, aur offline bhi kaam karta hai.

Q: TOTP phishing-proof hai?

Poori tarah nahi — agar tum fake site pe code type kar do to attacker 30 second ke andar use kar sakta hai. Hardware key (FIDO2) ya passkey poori tarah phishing-proof hain, kyunki wo galat domain pe kaam hi nahi karte.

8. Quick check

Sawaal 1: TOTP code kis cheez se banta hai?

  • Internet se aata hai
  • Shared secret + current time se, phone me locally [sahi jawab]
  • Server se SMS se
  • Fingerprint se

Sawaal 2: Phone kho jaye to TOTP account kaise recover karein?

  • Kuch nahi ho sakta
  • Backup codes ya recovery flow se [sahi jawab]
  • SMS se code aayega
  • Password se hi login ho jayega
Ek line me yaad rakh lo: TOTP = shared secret + time → 6-digit code, phone me locally banta hai, bina internet ke; SMS OTP se behtar (SIM swap-proof); backup codes zaroor save karo; hardware key/passkey usse bhi behtar hai.

Do stages — setup aur login, step by step

Google Authenticator two-step verification hai, isme 2 stages hote hain:

Stage 1 — Two-step verification enable karna:

  1. User web page khol kar two-step verification enable karta hai. Frontend secret key maangta hai.
  2. Authentication service secret key generate karti hai aur database me store karti hai.
  3. Service ek URI wapas bhejti hai — isme key issuer, username aur secret key hote hain. URI web page par QR code ki form me dikhta hai.
  4. User Google Authenticator se QR code scan karta hai — secret key authenticator me store ho jati hai.

Stage 2 — Login karna:

  1. User password daalta hai. Har 30 second me Google Authenticator TOTP (Time-based One Time Password) algorithm se 6-digit code banata hai.
  2. Frontend code backend ko bhejta hai. Authentication service database se secret key padh kar wahi TOTP algorithm se 6-digit code banati hai.
  3. Dono codes compare hote hain — match hue to hi login aage badhta hai.

Kya ye mechanism safe hai? Secret key HTTPS se hi bhejni chahiye; authenticator aur database dono me secret key encrypted store honi chahiye. 6-digit code ke 1 million combinations hote hain aur code har 30 second me badal jata hai — guess karne ke liye hacker ko 30 second me 30,000 combinations per second try karne padenge, jo practically possible nahi hai.

Source:https://github.com/ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/blob/main/data/guides/how-does-google-authenticator-or-other-types-of-2-factor-authenticators-work.md
← PichhlaHow Does a VPN Work?Agla →How does HTTPS work?
17Security (Part 1)

How does HTTPS work?

Har roz tum https:// wali sites kholte ho — par iske peeche kya hota hai? HTTPS = HTTP + TLS. Is page me poora flow samjho: DNS se leke certificate verify karne tak, aur key exchange se leke encrypted data tak — bilkul shuruaat se.

1. HTTPS — do doston ki secret baat-cheet

Socho tum aur tumhara dost bheed me khade ho aur secret baat karna chahte ho. Pehle tum dost ki pehchan verify karte ho (wo wahi hai na?), phir tum dono ek secret code tay karte ho (bina bole, ishaaron se), phir usi code me baat karte ho — aas-paas khade log sun to sakte hain, par samajh nahi sakte.

HTTPS wahi karta hai: pehchan (certificate), secret code (TLS handshake se session key), aur encrypted baat (AES se data). HTTP me ye teeno me se kuch nahi tha — sab khula postcard tha.

2. Gehrai me samjho — ek-ek point

Step 0 — DNS aur TCP connection

HTTPS shuru hone se pehle do kaam hote hain: DNS lookup — google.com ka IP address nikalo. TCP connection — us IP se port 443 pe connect karo (three-way handshake: SYN, SYN-ACK, ACK).

Uske baad TLS handshake shuru hota hai. Note: DNS query aam taur pe plain hoti hai — isliye ISP ko pata chal jata hai tum kis site pe gaye (DNS over HTTPS se ye bhi encrypt hota hai).

Step 1 — TLS Handshake

ClientHello: Browser kehta hai 'Main TLS 1.3 support karta hoon, ye mere ciphers hain, ye mera random number aur key share hai.'

ServerHello + Certificate: Server cipher chunta hai, apna random number, key share aur certificate bhejta hai (domain + public key + CA signature).

Verify: Browser certificate check karta hai — CA trusted hai? Domain match karta hai? Expiry theek hai? Sab theek ho to aage badho.

Key exchange: Dono ECDHE se shared secret banate hain — session keys tay ho gayi. Finished: Dono ek doosre ko 'handshake poora' ka encrypted message bhejte hain.

TLS 1.3 me ye sab 1 round trip me hota hai — fast aur secure.

Step 2 — Encrypted HTTP

Handshake ke baad jo bhi HTTP request/response hogi, wo AES encryption ke andar jayegi. URL, headers, cookies, body — sab encrypted.

Har message ke saath integrity check (AEAD) hota hai — beech me koi badal nahi sakta. Session keys har connection ke liye alag hoti hain — ek connection hack hua to doosra safe (forward secrecy).

Connection band hone par keys delete ho jati hain — agli visit pe naya handshake, nayi keys.

Certificate — kaun bharosa dilata hai?

Certificate Certificate Authority (CA) deta hai. Browser me trusted CAs ki list pehle se hoti hai (root certificates). Server ka certificate ek chain hoti hai: server cert → intermediate CA → root CA.

Let's Encrypt free certificates deta hai — isliye aaj har chhoti site bhi HTTPS use kar sakti hai. Certificate Transparency logs me har certificate public hota hai — koi chhup ke fake certificate nahi bana sakta.

Expiry: Certificates 90 din (Let's Encrypt) ya 1 saal ke hote hain — expire hone par browser warning dikhata hai. Auto-renewal lagana zaroori hai.

3. Poora HTTPS flow — ek saath

1. DNS: google.com → 142.250.80.46
2. TCP: port 443 pe connect (SYN, SYN-ACK, ACK)
3. TLS Handshake (1 round trip, TLS 1.3):
   Browser → Server: ClientHello (ciphers + key share)
   Server → Browser: ServerHello + Certificate + key share + Finished
   Browser: certificate verify ✓ → session keys banao
   Browser → Server: Finished
4. Encrypted HTTP:
   Browser → Server: GET / (AES encrypted)
   Server → Browser: 200 OK + HTML (AES encrypted)
5. Connection band → keys delete

# Jo dikhta hai bahar wale ko:
# - DNS: google.com (agar DoH nahi hai)
# - IP: 142.250.80.46, port 443
# - Baaki sab: encrypted kachra — URL path, cookies, data — kuch nahi dikhta

4. Try karo — ek HTTPS connection banao

Browser bano: google.com kholo aur har step dekho. Phir ek HTTP site aur ek fake certificate wali site bhi try karo.

5. HTTPS ke components — ek table me

ComponentKaam
HTTPRequest/response ka format (GET, POST...)
TLSEncryption + authentication layer
CertificateServer ki pehchan (CA signed)
ECDHEKey exchange (forward secrecy ke saath)
AESBulk data encryption (fast)
HSTSBrowser ko hamesha HTTPS pe rehne ko kehta hai

6. Common galtiyan — ye mat karna

  1. HTTPS ko 'site safe hai' samajhna: Phishing sites bhi HTTPS use karti hain. Domain check karo.
  2. Certificate expire hone dena: Expired certificate = browser warning = users bhaag jayenge. Auto-renewal lagao.
  3. Mixed content: HTTPS page pe HTTP script/image load karna — attacker use badal sakta hai. Sab kuch HTTPS pe rakho.
  4. TLS 1.0/1.1 chalana: Purane versions me jaani kamzoriyan hain. Minimum TLS 1.2, behtar 1.3.
  5. HSTS na lagana: Bina HSTS ke pehli visit pe attacker HTTP pe dhakel sakta hai (SSL stripping).

7. Interview corner

Q: HTTPS kaise kaam karta hai?

HTTPS = HTTP + TLS. Pehle DNS aur TCP connect hota hai, phir TLS handshake: ClientHello/ServerHello, server certificate bhejta hai jise browser verify karta hai, ECDHE se shared secret banta hai, phir saara HTTP data AES se encrypt hokar jata hai.

Q: TLS handshake me certificate ka kya kaam hai?

Certificate server ki pehchan sabit karta hai — isme server ka domain aur public key hoti hai, ek trusted CA ke signature ke saath. Browser chain verify karta hai: CA trusted hai, domain match karta hai, expiry theek hai. Tabhi aage badhta hai.

Q: HTTP aur HTTPS me farq?

HTTP plain text me hota hai — beech me koi bhi padh/badal sakta hai. HTTPS me TLS layer data ko encrypt karti hai, integrity check deti hai, aur certificate se server ki pehchan verify hoti hai.

8. Quick check

Sawaal 1: HTTPS me data encrypt karne ke liye kaunsa algorithm use hota hai (bulk data)?

  • RSA
  • AES (symmetric) [sahi jawab]
  • MD5
  • Base64

Sawaal 2: TLS handshake me server kya bhejta hai apni pehchan sabit karne ke liye?

  • Password
  • Certificate (CA signed) [sahi jawab]
  • IP address
  • Cookie
Ek line me yaad rakh lo: HTTPS = HTTP + TLS: DNS → TCP → TLS handshake (certificate verify + ECDHE key exchange) → AES encrypted data; taala matlab connection secure hai, site trustworthy hai ye guarantee nahi.
Source:https://github.com/ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/blob/main/data/guides/how-does-https-work.md

18Security (Part 1)

Explaining JSON Web Token (JWT) to a 10 Year Old Kid

JWT ko ek 10 saal ke bachche ko samjhana ho to kya kahoge? Is page me JWT ko bilkul simple bhasha me samjho — mela, toffee aur secret stamp ki kahani se. Aur haan, simple hone ka matlab halka nahi hai — andar poora technical depth bhi hai.

1. JWT — mele ka ticket wali kahani

Socho tum ek mele me gaye. Gate pe tumne ticket kharida — ticket pe likha hai: tumhara naam, tum VIP ho ya normal, aur ticket kab tak chalega. Neeche mele wale ki mohar (stamp) lagi hai.

Ab tum har ride pe jaate ho — jhoola, train, magic show. Har ride wala tumhara ticket dekhta hai: naam padhta hai, VIP hai ya nahi dekhta hai, expiry dekhta hai, aur mohar check karta hai. Mohar asli hai to andar jaane deta hai — use gate pe phone karke poochne ki zaroorat nahi padti: 'Ye ticket asli hai?'

JWT wahi ticket hai: naam + role + expiry ticket (payload) pe likhe hain, aur mohar (signature) server ki hai. Har API (ride) ticket dekh ke, mohar check karke andar jaane deti hai — bina server se poochhe.

Bachche ko samjhane wali line: JWT ek aisa ticket hai jisme sab kuch likha hota hai, aur uspe ek aisi mohar hoti hai jise koi nakli nahi bana sakta.

2. Gehrai me samjho — ek-ek point

Ticket ke 3 hisse

1) Header — ticket ka type: 'Ye kis type ka ticket hai, aur mohar kaunsi wali hai?' {"alg": "HS256", "typ": "JWT"}

2) Payload — ticket pe kya likha hai: Tumhara naam, tum kaun ho (user id), tum VIP ho ya nahi (role), ticket kab tak chalega (expiry). {"name": "Priya", "role": "user", "exp": 1516239922}

3) Signature — mohar: Ticket pe likhi cheezon ko server ne apni secret mohar se stamp kiya. Koi ticket pe likha badal de to mohar match nahi karegi — nakli ticket pakda jayega.

Teeno hisse dot (.) se jude hote hain: header.payload.signature — jaise ticket ke 3 tukde ek saath chipke hon.

Ticket kaise banta hai? (Login)

1) Tum gate pe jaate ho (login karte ho) — password dete ho. 2) Gate wala check karta hai — password sahi hai. 3) Wo tumhara ticket banata hai: naam, role, expiry likhta hai, aur apni secret mohar lagata hai. 4) Ticket tumhe de deta hai — tum use apni jeb me rakhte ho (browser/mobile app).

Ab tumhe har ride pe password nahi dena padta — sirf ticket dikhana padta hai. Password ek baar diya, ticket baar-baar kaam aaya.

Ticket kaise check hota hai? (Har request)

Har ride (API) pe tum ticket dikhate ho: Authorization: Bearer <ticket>. Ride wala: (1) Ticket ke 3 hisse alag karta hai. (2) Mohar dobara banata hai apne secret se — match hui to ticket asli hai. (3) Expiry dekhta hai — ticket expire to nahi hua? (4) Payload padhta hai — 'Priya hai, role user hai' — theek hai, andar aao.

Ride wale ko gate pe phone nahi karna padta — isliye ye fast hai aur scale karta hai. Hazaar rides, ek bhi phone call nahi.

Ticket ki kamzoriyan — bachche ko bhi samjhao

1) Ticket kho jaye to? Koi bhi use kar sakta hai — jab tak expiry na ho. Isliye ticket ki expiry chhoti rakho (15 minute) aur ek alag 'refresh ticket' rakho.

2) Ticket pe likha sab koi padh sakta hai: Ticket khula hai — koi bhi padh sakta hai kya likha hai (naam, role). Isliye ticket pe secret cheezein (password) kabhi mat likho.

3) Ticket wapas nahi liya ja sakta: Ek baar ticket de diya to gate wala use turant cancel nahi kar sakta — use expiry ka intezaar karna padta hai. Isliye logout ke baad bhi ticket thodi der kaam karta hai.

Sahi: Chhoti expiry + refresh token = ticket kho bhi jaye to nuksaan kam.

3. Asli JWT dekho — decode karke

Ek asli JWT (jwt.io pe paste karo):
eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9
.eyJzdWIiOiIxMjM0IiwibmFtZSI6IlByaXlhIiwicm9sZSI6InVzZXIiLCJleHAiOjE1MTYyMzk5MjJ9
.SflKxwRJSMeKKF2QT4fwpMeJf36POk6yJV_adQssw5c

Hissa 1 (Header):  {"alg": "HS256", "typ": "JWT"}
Hissa 2 (Payload): {"sub": "1234", "name": "Priya",
                    "role": "user", "exp": 1516239922}
Hissa 3 (Signature): secret key se bani mohar — sirf server jaanta hai

# Payload ko koi bhi padh sakta hai (Base64 decode) —
# par mohar sirf server bana sakta hai (secret key se)!

4. Try karo — mele ka ticket banao

Tum mele ke gate wale ho. Ek bachche ko ticket banao, phir alag-alag situations me ticket check karo — nakli ticket, expired ticket, khoya ticket.

5. JWT ko bachche ko samjhane ke 5 points

#PointSimple bhasha
1JWT ek ticket haiNaam, role, expiry likhi hoti hai
2Uspe mohar hoti haiSignature — nakli nahi ban sakti
3Har jagah dikhaoHar request pe Authorization header me
4Koi phone nahi kartaServer ko lookup nahi karna — stateless
5Ticket kho jaye to?Expiry chhoti rakho + refresh token

6. Common galtiyan — ye mat karna

  1. Bachche ko technical jargon se samjhana: 'Base64URL encoded JSON' nahi — 'ticket pe likha hai' kaho. Pehle kahani, phir technical terms.
  2. JWT ko 'encrypted' kehna: Ticket khula hai — koi bhi padh sakta hai. Mohar sirf authenticity deti hai, confidentiality nahi.
  3. Ticket ki expiry bhoolna: Bina expiry ke ticket hamesha kaam karega — kho jaye to koi bhi use kar sakta hai.
  4. Ticket pe secret likhna: Password ya personal data payload me kabhi mat likho — koi bhi padh sakta hai.
  5. Ticket ko logout se cancel samajhna: Ticket server se cancel nahi hota — expiry ka intezaar karna padta hai, ya refresh token revoke karna padta hai.

7. Interview corner

Q: JWT ko ek 10 saal ke bachche ko kaise samjhaoge?

JWT ek mele ka ticket hai — uspe tumhara naam, tum VIP ho ya nahi, aur ticket kab tak chalega, likha hota hai. Neeche mele wale ki mohar hoti hai jise koi nakli nahi bana sakta. Har ride wala ticket dekh ke, mohar check karke andar jaane deta hai — use gate pe phone nahi karna padta.

Q: JWT stateless kyun hai?

Kyunki server ko ticket verify karne ke liye kisi register ya database ko dekhne ki zaroorat nahi — signature verify karo, payload padho, ho gaya. Isliye JWT fast hai aur scale karta hai.

Q: JWT ka sabse bada trade-off kya hai?

Revoke karna mushkil hai — ek baar ticket de diya to expiry tak valid rehta hai. Isliye expiry chhoti rakhte hain (15 min) aur refresh token alag se use karte hain, jise server revoke kar sakta hai.

8. Quick check

Sawaal 1: JWT me signature (mohar) ka kya kaam hai?

  • Ticket ko chhupana
  • Ye sabit karna ki ticket asli hai aur badla nahi gaya [sahi jawab]
  • Ticket ko fast banana
  • Password store karna

Sawaal 2: JWT ka payload koi bhi kyun padh sakta hai?

  • Payload encrypt hota hai
  • Payload sirf Base64 encoded hota hai — decode karna aasan hai [sahi jawab]
  • Payload server pe rehta hai
  • Payload khaali hota hai
Ek line me yaad rakh lo: JWT = mele ka ticket: naam + role + expiry (payload) aur secret mohar (signature); har API mohar check karke andar jaane deti hai, bina server se poochhe; expiry chhoti rakho, sensitive data payload me mat likho.
Source:https://github.com/ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/blob/main/data/guides/explaining-json-web-token-jwt-to-a-10-year-old-kid.md

Interactive Labs

4 labs — mushkil concepts ko haath se aazmao. Har lab ka output yahin live dikhta hai.

LABJWT Inspector — token ko khol kar dekho

Neeche ek JWT hai. Decode dabao aur dekho header aur payload ke andar kya hai — aur 2 galat tokens bhi try karo: ek expired, ek alg=none wala. Asli JWT me signature secret se verify hota hai; yahan hum sirf decode kar rahe hain, verify nahi.

Decode dabao — header, payload aur warnings yahan dikhenge.
LABPassword Hashing Lab — salt ka jaadu

Ek hi password ko 2 alag salt ke saath hash karo aur dekho — hash poora alag banta hai. Yehi wajah hai ki leaked database me bhi attacker ko har password alag se crack karna padta hai. (Ye ek demo hash hai — asli bcrypt/Argon2 nahi, sirf concept dikhane ke liye.)

Hash karo dabao.
LABHTTPS Handshake Stepper — TLS ka safar

Browser se server tak HTTPS connection kaise banta hai — steps ko order me chalao. Phir MITM (man-in-the-middle) attack try karo aur dekho certificate verification kaise bachata hai.

Step 1 se shuru karo.
LABOAuth 2.0 Flow Simulator — login ka safar

Google se login karne par andar kya hota hai — authorization code flow ko step by step chalao. PKCE on/off karke dekho, aur purana Implicit flow kyun deprecated hai, wo bhi samjho.

Flow chuno aur chalao.
