Interview FAQs

12 FAQs — aaj ke era ke system design interviews me poochhe jaane wale sawaal, seedhe jawab ke saath. Sawaal par tap karo, jawab khulega.

01Authentication aur authorization me kya farq hai, aur interview me iska example kaise dein?
Authentication ye prove karta hai ki tum kaun ho — jaise login karte waqt password ya OTP se identity verify karna. Authorization ye decide karta hai ki verified user ko kya-kya karne ki permission hai — jaise ek normal user settings badal sakta hai par admin panel nahi khol sakta. Short me: authentication = "tum kaun ho?", authorization = "tum kya kar sakte ho?" Interview me example do: Google login karna authentication hai; login ke baad sirf apni Drive files dekh paana authorization hai. Dono ko hamesha alag rakho — pehle pehchan, phir permission.
02Symmetric aur asymmetric encryption me kya farq hai, aur kab kaunsa use karna chahiye?
Symmetric encryption me ek hi key se encrypt aur decrypt hota hai (jaise AES) — ye bahut fast hai, isliye bade data ko encrypt karne ke liye use hota hai. Problem ye hai ki key ko dono taraf safely pahunchana padta hai. Asymmetric encryption me key pair hota hai — public key se encrypt, private key se decrypt (jaise RSA) — ye slow hai par key exchange ki problem solve karta hai. Practically dono ek saath use hote hain: HTTPS handshake me asymmetric se session key exchange hoti hai, phir poora data symmetric (AES) se encrypt hota hai. Interview me ye hybrid approach bolna zaroori hai.
03HTTPS man-in-the-middle (MITM) attack se kaise bachata hai?
HTTPS 2 cheezon se bachata hai. Pehla, TLS handshake me server apna certificate bhejta hai jisme uski public key aur CA (Certificate Authority) ki signature hoti hai — browser CA ki public key se signature verify karta hai, to attacker ka fake certificate pakda jata hai aur browser warning dikha kar connection rok deta hai. Doosra, handshake ke baad saara data session keys se encrypted hota hai, to beech me baitha attacker data padh nahi sakta aur badal bhi nahi sakta (integrity). Sirf encryption hota to kaafi nahi hota — certificate verification hi asli MITM protection hai.
04JWT aur session cookie me kya farq hai — kab kaunsa chunein?
Session cookie me server session id banata hai aur session ka data apne paas (database ya Redis) store karta hai — cookie me sirf id hoti hai, isliye cookie chhoti aur safe hoti hai, aur logout par server session delete kar deta hai. JWT me saara data token ke payload me hota hai aur server ko kuch store nahi karna padta — ye stateless aur scalable hai, par token bada hota hai, expiry se pehle revoke karna mushkil hai, aur payload sirf base64 hota hai (encrypted nahi), to sensitive data kabhi payload me mat rakho. Rule: same domain ki web app ke liye session cookie, mobile apps aur microservices ke liye short-lived JWT + refresh token.
05OAuth 2.0 authorization code flow kaise kaam karta hai?
Authorization code flow me 4 parties hote hain: user, client app, authorization server (jaise Google) aur resource server. Step 1: user "Google se login karo" dabata hai, browser Google par redirect hota hai. Step 2: user Google par login karke consent deta hai. Step 3: Google ek authorization code lekar app par wapas bhejta hai — code akele bekaar hai. Step 4: client code + apna secret server-to-server Google ko bhejta hai aur access token leta hai. Step 5: token se resource server se user data milta hai. Is flow ki khaasiyat: user ka password app ko kabhi pata nahi chalta, aur token browser se nahi, server se exchange hota hai. PKCE add karne se code intercept hone par bhi token safe rehta hai.
06Passwords ko database me kaise store karna chahiye?
Password ko kabhi plain text me aur kabhi sirf encryption se store mat karo — encryption reversible hota hai, key leak hui to saare passwords khul jayenge. Sahi tareeka: password + unique salt ko slow hash function (bcrypt ya Argon2) se hash karo aur hash + salt store karo. Salt har user ke liye alag hota hai, isliye 2 users ka same password hone par bhi hash alag banta hai aur rainbow table attack fail ho jata hai. Slow hash (bcrypt cost factor, Argon2 memory-hard) brute force ko mehenga bana deta hai. Login par: user ka password dobara usi salt se hash karo, stored hash se match karo — match hua to allow. Password validate karte waqt timing attack se bachne ke liye constant-time comparison use karo.
07SQL injection kya hai aur isse kaise bachein?
SQL injection me attacker input field (jaise login form) me SQL code daal deta hai jo database query ka hissa ban jata hai — jaise username me "admin' --" daal kar password check ko bypass kar dena, ya "OR 1=1" se poori table nikal lena. Isse bachne ka sabse solid tareeka hai parameterized queries (prepared statements) — user input ko kabhi query string me concatenate mat karo, use parameter ki tarah pass karo, taaki database use data samjhe, code nahi. Uske saath input validation, least-privilege database user (app ko sirf zaroori tables ka access), aur WAF add karo. ORM use karna bhi madad karta hai, par raw queries likhte waqt prepared statements hi asli defense hai.
08XSS aur CSRF me kya farq hai aur inhe kaise rokte hain?
XSS (Cross-Site Scripting) me attacker tumhari site par apna JavaScript inject karta hai jo doosre users ke browser me chal jata hai — jaise comment box me script tag daal dena, jo phir cookies chura le. Rokne ke liye: user input ko output par escape karo, Content-Security-Policy header lagao, aur cookies par HttpOnly flag lagao taaki JavaScript cookie padh na sake. CSRF (Cross-Site Request Forgery) me attacker user ko dhokhe se tumhari site par request karwa deta hai — jaise ek malicious page se bank ki transfer request, jo user ki logged-in cookie ke saath jati hai. Rokne ke liye: har state-changing request par CSRF token check karo, aur cookies par SameSite=Lax ya Strict lagao. Short me: XSS tumhare page me code ghusata hai, CSRF tumhare user se request karwata hai.
09Digital signature encryption se kaise alag hai, aur ye kaise kaam karta hai?
Encryption ka kaam hai data ko chhupana — sirf wahi padhe jiske paas key hai. Digital signature ka kaam hai authenticity aur integrity prove karna — ye batata hai ki message kisne bheja aur beech me badla to nahi. Kaam aise karta hai: sender message ka hash banata hai aur use apni private key se encrypt (sign) karta hai — yehi signature hai. Receiver message ka hash dobara banata hai aur sender ki public key se signature ko decrypt karke hash se milata hai — match hua to message asli hai aur unchanged hai. Isliye signature me private key se sign aur public key se verify hota hai — encryption se ulta. Non-repudiation bhi milta hai: sender baad me mana nahi kar sakta ki usne bheja nahi.
102FA aur TOTP kaise kaam karta hai, aur ye SMS OTP se behtar kyun hai?
2FA me login ke liye 2 cheezein chahiye: kuch jo tum jaante ho (password) aur kuch jo tumhare paas hai (phone/app). TOTP (Time-based One Time Password) me setup ke waqt server aur authenticator app ek secret key share karte hain. Har 30 second me dono taraf se secret + current time se 6-digit code banta hai — server apna code tumhare code se milata hai. Code har 30 second me badalta hai aur offline banta hai. SMS OTP se behtar isliye hai: SMS SIM swap attack se hijack ho sakta hai, network par intercept ho sakta hai, aur SMS delivery par depend karta hai; TOTP me secret device par rehta hai aur code kabhi network par nahi jata. Isliye authenticator app ya hardware key, SMS OTP se zyada safe mani jati hai.
11Firewall aur WAF me kya farq hai, aur dono kahan lagte hain?
Firewall network layer par kaam karta hai — ye packets ko IP, port aur protocol dekh kar allow ya block karta hai, jaise ghar ke gate par guard. Ye network ke entry point par lagta hai. WAF (Web Application Firewall) application layer (Layer 7) par kaam karta hai — ye HTTP requests ko samajhta hai aur SQL injection, XSS jaise application attacks ko block karta hai, jaise gate ke andar ek aur guard jo har visitor ki baat-cheet sunta hai. Firewall bina dekhe ki packet ke andar kya hai, allow/block karta hai; WAF packet ke andar ka HTTP content analyze karta hai. Production me dono lagte hain: firewall pehle network-level filtering karta hai, phir WAF application-level attacks rokta hai.
12RBAC vs ABAC — permission system kaise design karein, aur kab kaunsa chunein?
RBAC (Role-Based Access Control) me permissions roles ko milti hain aur users ko roles milte hain — jaise Admin, Editor, Viewer. Ye simple aur samajhne me easy hai, aur zyada tar apps ke liye kaafi hai. ABAC (Attribute-Based Access Control) me permission resource owner, action, resource aur environment ke attributes dekh kar decide hoti hai — jaise "sirf usi department ka manager apne department ki file edit kar sakta hai, aur sirf office hours me". ABAC bahut flexible hai par rules complex ho jate hain aur implement karna mushkil hai. Interview me bolo: chhote-medium system me RBAC se shuru karo; jab permissions attributes par depend karne lagen (department, location, time, sensitivity) tab ABAC ya RBAC+ABAC hybrid use karo. Permission check hamesha server side karo, kabhi sirf UI par hide karke mat chhodo.
